template_name: Procedural Gateway Before Merits
description: Determines whether a procedural prerequisite must be satisfied before the court can examine the underlying contractual rights and obligations.
application_scenario: Use when a contract-related claim is accompanied by a threshold question concerning jurisdiction, service, leave, timing, standing, appealability, or another condition governing whether the merits may be reached.
reasoning_flow: Identify the requested judicial action and the procedural route by which it is sought.
Extract each legal prerequisite that must be satisfied before substantive adjudication.
Match the record to those prerequisites and identify any unresolved threshold facts.
Separate threshold facts from facts relevant only to contractual liability.
Proceed to the merits only for issues that remain justiciable after the threshold assessment.
example_application: A claimant seeks contractual relief, but the responding party challenges the court's power to hear the matter. Apply the governing gateway requirements first, then analyze performance or breach only if the gateway permits merits review.

template_name: Procedural Posture and Decision Standard
description: Selects the decision standard associated with the current procedural posture rather than treating every application as a full trial on liability.
application_scenario: Use for summary procedures, interlocutory applications, appeals, rehearings, strike-out requests, leave applications, and other settings where the court applies a posture-specific test.
reasoning_flow: Classify the proceeding by its present procedural posture and requested order.
Identify the governing threshold, burden, and permissible scope of factual determination.
Distinguish questions that may be decided at this stage from questions reserved for later adjudication.
Assess the materials using the posture-specific standard rather than a final-liability standard.
Record which issues can be resolved procedurally and which require a different stage of proceedings.
example_application: A creditor invokes an expedited procedure based on written payment instruments. The analysis first asks what must be shown at that stage and whether disputed facts require fuller adjudication, rather than immediately deciding ultimate liability.

template_name: Material Fact Chronology Filter
description: Converts a lengthy factual record into a chronology limited to events that affect the procedural threshold or the disputed contractual obligation.
application_scenario: Use when the record contains extended negotiations, documents, payments, communications, procedural steps, or later conduct, but only part of that history bears on the live issues.
reasoning_flow: State the live procedural and substantive issues in neutral terms.
Arrange potentially relevant events in chronological order.
Retain facts that change a legal element, deadline, party position, evidentiary status, or available remedy.
Exclude background details that do not affect any identified issue.
Link each retained fact to the issue or element for which it is material.
example_application: The parties exchanged numerous communications before and after an alleged default. Build a focused timeline showing formation, required performance, alleged nonperformance, subsequent communications, and the procedural application now before the court.

template_name: Dependent Multi-Issue Sequencing
description: Orders multiple issues so that foundational questions are resolved before dependent questions about breach, defenses, procedure, or remedy.
application_scenario: Use when a case presents two or more connected issues, such as authority before enforceability, breach before waiver, title before possession, or substantive liability before procedural relief.
reasoning_flow: List each distinct legal issue without merging separate tests.
Identify which issues are logically or legally prerequisites for others.
Place threshold and foundational issues before derivative liability or remedy issues.
Carry forward only the findings needed by each dependent issue.
Check whether resolution of an earlier issue makes any later inquiry unnecessary or changes its scope.
example_application: A dispute raises whether an agreement was validly made and whether a party later failed to perform it. Analyze valid formation first because the performance question depends on the existence and scope of an enforceable obligation.

template_name: Rule-to-Element Extraction and Mapping
description: Transforms supplied legislation, contractual provisions, procedural rules, or authorities into an operational element checklist and maps the record to each element.
application_scenario: Use when governing legal text is supplied but the case materials do not already organize it into a usable test.
reasoning_flow: Identify the legal source governing the specific issue and procedural posture.
Extract mandatory elements, exceptions, definitions, deadlines, and discretionary factors.
Assign the applicable burden for each contested requirement.
Map material facts and evidentiary gaps to the extracted requirements.
Keep rule interpretation separate from factual application and note any ambiguity requiring authority or analogy.
example_application: A procedural rule authorizes an order only when several stated conditions are met. Convert those conditions into a checklist, assign the relevant facts to each condition, and isolate any missing or disputed requirement.

template_name: Summary Disposition Triable-Issue Screen
description: Screens whether an asserted defense or factual dispute is sufficiently concrete and legally material to require fuller adjudication under a summary procedure.
application_scenario: Use when a party seeks summary judgment or comparable expedited determination and the opposing party relies on alleged oral terms, conditional delivery, duress, lack of consideration, misrepresentation, authority, or another defense.
reasoning_flow: Identify the applicant's prima facie contractual or payment case.
List each defense or factual dispute advanced in response.
Test whether each response is legally material to an element of the claim or a recognized defense.
Examine whether the response has a coherent factual basis and admissible evidentiary foundation.
Distinguish a genuine issue requiring fuller adjudication from a bare assertion, inconsistency, or immaterial dispute.
example_application: A written payment claim is met by an allegation that delivery was conditional and that later conversations altered the obligation. Evaluate whether those allegations are legally relevant, factually particularized, and grounded in evidence sufficient for the applicable summary-stage threshold.

template_name: Jurisdiction, Service, and Territorial Nexus Check
description: Assesses whether the court has a sufficient legal and factual connection to the parties or dispute and whether the initiating process was validly served.
application_scenario: Use when jurisdiction depends on residence, business presence, statutory connection, service rules, forum suitability, or a party's relationship with the territory.
reasoning_flow: Identify the asserted statutory or procedural basis for jurisdiction and service.
Separate subject-matter jurisdiction, personal or territorial nexus, service validity, and forum suitability.
Extract facts showing residence, presence, business activity, contractual connection, or other required nexus.
Apply any statutory definition or service condition to those facts.
Determine whether defects in one jurisdictional component prevent the action from advancing regardless of the contractual merits.
example_application: A foreign-connected contracting party contests service and argues that the forum lacks a sufficient nexus. Analyze the legal basis for jurisdiction, the party's relevant territorial activities, and compliance with the service mechanism before reaching the contract claim.

template_name: Late Evidence or Pleading Change Prejudice Assessment
description: Balances the relevance of late material or a proposed pleading change against delay, prejudice, explanation, and the ability to preserve a fair hearing.
application_scenario: Use for late disclosure, supplemental witness evidence, amendment of pleadings, vacation of a hearing date, or other procedural changes sought after the case has substantially progressed.
reasoning_flow: Identify the new evidence, allegation, or procedural change and the issue it is said to affect.
Assess its apparent relevance and potential significance to the live dispute.
Examine the explanation for lateness and whether the material could reasonably have been produced earlier.
Identify concrete prejudice, including lost preparation time, unavailable evidence, added cost, or disruption of the hearing.
Consider whether directions, limited adjournment, costs, or narrowed use of the material can address the prejudice.
example_application: Important accounting material appears shortly before trial and one party seeks to rely on it while the other requests more preparation time. Assess significance, lateness, prejudice, and available case-management measures together.

template_name: Evidence Admissibility, Credibility, and Burden Matrix
description: Separates whether evidence may be considered, what weight it deserves, and which party bears the consequence of any evidentiary gap.
application_scenario: Use when a contract dispute turns on oral evidence, documentary inconsistency, conditional delivery, alleged later agreements, disputed authority, or the credibility of negotiations and conduct.
reasoning_flow: Identify the proposition for which each disputed item of evidence is offered.
Apply any rule limiting admissibility, including restrictions on contradicting or varying written terms.
If admissible, test internal consistency, contemporaneous corroboration, plausibility, and conduct consistent with the account.
Allocate the burden for the underlying contractual element or defense.
Assess the consequence of evidentiary uncertainty under the applicable procedural posture.
example_application: A party relies on oral conversations to qualify a written instrument and also points to later conduct. Analyze admissibility first, then credibility and corroboration, and finally the effect of any remaining uncertainty under the assigned burden.

template_name: Discretionary Relief Factor Balancing
description: Structures the assessment of relief that depends on judicial discretion after any mandatory legal thresholds have been addressed.
application_scenario: Use for interim injunctions, security for costs, leave applications, extensions, setting aside agreements, or other orders requiring a balance of identified factors rather than automatic relief.
reasoning_flow: Identify mandatory gateway requirements and assess them before discretionary factors.
Specify the interests the requested order would protect and the harms it could impose.
Evaluate urgency, adequacy of alternative relief, preservation of the status quo, delay, and conduct where relevant.
Consider proportionality and whether a narrower order could address the demonstrated risk.
State the factor balance without substituting the merits analysis for the discretionary test.
example_application: A claimant seeks an interim order affecting possession while the contractual dispute remains unresolved. Examine the legal gateway, comparative risks, available alternatives, and proportional scope of any temporary measure.

template_name: Subsequent Conduct as Waiver, Affirmation, or Variation
description: Evaluates whether post-breach words or conduct changed the parties' contractual positions through waiver, affirmation, election, or an agreed variation.
application_scenario: Use when a party allegedly continued negotiations, accepted performance, requested further performance, made a later promise, or otherwise acted inconsistently with immediate reliance on an earlier breach.
reasoning_flow: Identify the original contractual obligation and the alleged breach or triggering event.
Identify the legal doctrine invoked to characterize the later conduct.
Isolate communications and acts occurring after the relevant event.
Test whether the conduct was clear, informed, attributable to the party, and consistent with the requirements of the invoked doctrine.
Define the resulting effect on existing rights, future performance, and any remaining remedy without assuming that all later dealings alter the contract.
example_application: After an alleged repudiation, the other party continues discussing completion and requests further steps. Determine whether that conduct merely explored settlement or instead amounted to an election, waiver, affirmation, or agreed change in obligations.

template_name: Contract Authority and Transaction Characterization
description: Tests whether the person or entity said to have contracted had authority and whether the transaction had the legal character asserted by the claimant.
application_scenario: Use when the dispute concerns actual or apparent authority, an alleged sham, whether funds were loans or another type of transfer, or whether an oral arrangement created or changed contractual obligations.
reasoning_flow: Identify the alleged agreement, its asserted legal character, and the parties said to be bound.
Examine actual authority, apparent authority, ratification, or other attribution rules relevant to the contracting actor.
Compare the stated transaction with contemporaneous documents, payment flows, performance, and later conduct.
Test whether the alleged arrangement contains sufficiently definite terms and any required formalities.
Analyze enforceability and performance only after authority and transaction character have been established.
example_application: Funds were transferred through a company representative, but the recipient disputes both the representative's authority and the description of the transfer as a loan. Resolve attribution and transaction character before addressing repayment.

template_name: Reconstruct the Governing Contractual Framework
description: Identify the operative agreement and assemble the express, oral, supplemental, and incorporated terms that govern the disputed obligation.
application_scenario: Use when the parties rely on several documents, negotiations, later variations, or different levels of a contractual chain to define their rights and duties.
reasoning_flow: List each potentially operative agreement, amendment, incorporated document, and alleged oral term.
Identify the parties and transaction level to which each instrument applies.
Determine whether later instruments vary, preserve, or replace earlier terms.
Separate agreed terms from disputed assertions about what was promised.
State the resulting contractual framework before evaluating performance or breach.
example_application: A subcontractor invokes a clause contained in an upstream agreement, while the counterparty relies on a later work order. The analysis first determines which documents bind the two parties and whether the upstream clause became part of their own bargain.

template_name: Test Incorporation by Reference and Assent
description: Determine whether a term located in another document became binding through sufficiently clear reference, notice, and objective assent.
application_scenario: Use when a party invokes an arbitration clause, standard condition, deed, regulation, or upstream contract that is not reproduced in the signed instrument.
reasoning_flow: Identify the external document and the exact term said to be incorporated.
Examine the wording and specificity of the contractual reference to that document.
Determine whether the party to be bound had access to, notice of, or a fair opportunity to review the term.
Check whether the external term is compatible with the identities of the parties and the structure of their transaction.
Apply the governing incorporation rule and record any material mismatch that may limit the term's operation.
example_application: A service agreement refers generally to another contract containing a dispute-resolution clause drafted for different parties. The analysis tests the clarity of the reference, notice, and whether the clause can sensibly operate in the later agreement.

template_name: Map Performance Duties and Preconditions
description: Translate the contractual framework into concrete duties, dependencies, and implied obligations that must be satisfied before performance becomes due.
application_scenario: Use when completion depends on approvals, title documents, vacant possession, accounts, payment, cooperation, or another party's prior act.
reasoning_flow: Identify each party's principal promised performance.
List express conditions, external approvals, documentary requirements, and sequencing dependencies.
Determine whether duties of cooperation, expedition, disclosure, or non-obstruction arise by implication.
Separate true preconditions from terms that regulate only the manner or timing of performance.
Assess whether the relevant condition was satisfied, waived, prevented, or left outstanding when performance was demanded.
example_application: Completion of a transfer depends on regulatory consent and delivery of specified title material. The analysis determines whether those matters were prerequisites, whether reasonable steps were taken, and whether completion had become due.

template_name: Analyze Repudiation, Acceptance, and Termination Sequence
description: Evaluate whether conduct amounted to repudiation and whether the responding party validly accepted it or terminated under the contract.
application_scenario: Use when both sides accuse each other of wrongful termination, non-completion, refusal to deliver, suspension, or abandonment.
reasoning_flow: Fix the contractual performance date and any valid extension or time-of-essence term.
Identify the conduct alleged to show inability, refusal, or failure to perform.
Determine whether the conduct was sufficiently clear and serious when viewed in context.
Check whether the other party was itself ready, willing, and able to perform the reciprocal obligations then due.
Trace any notice, demand, cure opportunity, acceptance, or termination in chronological order.
Classify the legal effect of the sequence before turning to monetary or proprietary remedies.
example_application: A buyer refuses completion because required documents remain outstanding, and the seller then issues a termination notice. The analysis tests the seller's own readiness, the seriousness of the outstanding defect, and the legal effect of each communication.

template_name: Evaluate Tender, Cure, and Prevention of Performance
description: Assess whether a party made an adequate tender of performance, had a reasonable opportunity to cure, or was prevented from performing by the counterparty.
application_scenario: Use when performance was delayed or refused after requests for information, missing payment, documentary objections, inspection demands, or access problems.
reasoning_flow: Specify what valid performance required at the relevant time.
Compare the actual tender with the contractual standard, including timing, completeness, and accompanying documents.
Identify any objection and determine whether it was genuine, material, and communicated clearly.
Examine whether a reasonable cure opportunity was offered and whether cure occurred before termination.
Determine whether either party caused, obstructed, or materially contributed to the non-performance.
example_application: A supplier delays delivery after demanding additional identity information not required by the bargain, then later offers delivery. The analysis compares the tender with the contract and asks whether the supplier itself frustrated timely performance.

template_name: Calculate Expectation Loss Using Market and Resale Evidence
description: Measure expectation loss by selecting the legally relevant valuation date and weighing market evidence, resale evidence, credits, and consequential items.
application_scenario: Use after a failed sale or supply contract when the claimed loss depends on the difference between the contract position and the substitute transaction or market value.
reasoning_flow: Identify the breach or termination date that governs valuation.
Select the proper damages measure under the contract and governing doctrine.
Compare contemporaneous market valuations with any actual resale or substitute transaction.
Adjust for differences in condition, timing, comparables, and transaction circumstances.
Deduct deposits, part-payments, or other credits that must be brought into account.
Assess interest and consequential losses separately, excluding periods or items attributable to avoidable delay.
example_application: A seller resells an asset soon after the purchaser fails to complete, while experts give differing market values. The analysis identifies the correct valuation date, weighs the resale and expert evidence, and accounts for credits and consequential losses.

template_name: Assess Mitigation and Reasonableness of Substitute Transactions
description: Determine whether the claimant acted reasonably to reduce loss and whether a rapid resale, replacement purchase, or other substitute transaction fairly evidences the recoverable loss.
application_scenario: Use when the claimant quickly resells property, obtains replacement performance, delays action, or accepts the first available offer after breach.
reasoning_flow: Identify the steps taken after breach to reduce or contain loss.
Evaluate the information, urgency, and commercial constraints facing the claimant at that time.
Examine marketing, negotiation, timing, and available alternatives for the substitute transaction.
Distinguish a reasonable response from conduct that unnecessarily enlarged the loss.
Adjust the damages analysis only for loss that reasonable steps would probably have avoided.
example_application: An owner accepts the first resale offer shortly after a failed completion. The analysis considers market conditions, exposure to the market, bargaining efforts, and whether a different course would probably have reduced the loss.

template_name: Classify Deposits, Refunds, Forfeiture, and Restitution
description: Determine the legal character of money transferred under a contract and the consequences of termination, invalidity, failed performance, or mistake.
application_scenario: Use when a party seeks return or retention of deposits, purchase money, advances, or payments made under an ineffective or unperformed transaction.
reasoning_flow: Classify each payment as a true deposit, part-payment, loan, contribution, fee, or other transfer.
Identify the contractual and doctrinal basis claimed for retention or recovery.
Determine which party's conduct caused the transaction to fail and whether termination was valid.
Check statutory, equitable, or penalty-related limits on forfeiture or retention.
For restitution, identify enrichment, the transfer's basis, any mistake or failure of basis, and applicable defenses.
Account for benefits received, credits, and countervailing obligations before quantifying the monetary consequence.
example_application: A purchaser seeks repayment of money paid before completion, while the seller claims a right to retain it as a deposit. The analysis classifies the payment, tests the termination and forfeiture basis, and considers restitutionary alternatives.

template_name: Test Enforceability Against Vitiating Conduct and Equitable Bars
description: Evaluate whether misrepresentation, sham arrangements, collusion, estoppel, unconscionability, delay, or the claimant's own conduct affects enforcement or equitable relief.
application_scenario: Use when formal contractual rights are challenged by allegations that the transaction or enforcement conduct was misleading, artificial, unfair, inconsistent, or inequitable.
reasoning_flow: Identify the precise vitiating doctrine or equitable bar relied upon.
Break the doctrine into its required elements and allocate the relevant evidential burden.
Match contemporaneous communications, commercial behavior, and objective transaction structure to those elements.
Distinguish mere suspicion, irregularity, or hard bargaining from conduct satisfying the doctrine.
Determine whether the doctrine affects formation, enforceability, a particular term, or only the availability of discretionary relief.
example_application: A lender relies on a signed agreement, while the borrower alleges collusion and an oppressive effective rate. The analysis separately tests the alleged conduct and identifies whether any established defect affects the whole agreement or only a remedy.

template_name: Resolve Threshold Entitlement Before Reaching the Merits
description: Address standing, procedural competence, pleading sufficiency, genuine-dispute thresholds, and discretionary gateways before deciding the substantive contractual controversy.
application_scenario: Use when bankruptcy, representative capacity, amendment, winding-up, disclosure, validation, injunction, or another procedural gateway may control whether the claim or remedy can proceed.
reasoning_flow: Identify the threshold rule governing who may bring the claim and in what procedural form.
Determine whether the relevant right vested in another person, estate, officeholder, or entity.
Check whether the pleaded facts articulate each required basis for the claim and requested remedy.
Assess whether any dispute is genuine and substantial rather than merely asserted.
Separate jurisdictional or mandatory requirements from matters of judicial discretion.
Only after the gateway is satisfied, proceed to the underlying merits and remedy analysis.
example_application: A claimant seeks an exceptional corporate remedy while also pleading an alternative contractual claim. The analysis first tests standing, pleading completeness, and whether a genuine dispute or statutory gateway changes the proper procedural route.

template_name: Apply Precedent Through Material-Fact Analogy and Distinction
description: Use prior authority by extracting its governing proposition and comparing the material facts and legal function of the rule, rather than copying its result.
application_scenario: Use whenever competing authorities address similar contract language, performance failures, remedies, procedural thresholds, or factual settings.
reasoning_flow: Extract the legal proposition for which each authority is invoked.
Identify the material facts and procedural posture that made the proposition operative.
Map the present facts to those material features, noting both similarities and differences.
Determine whether any difference changes the rule's rationale, scope, or practical application.
Reconcile authorities at different levels of generality and give priority according to hierarchy and directness.
State the adapted rule for the present issue without importing the earlier case's ultimate disposition.
example_application: An earlier decision concerns termination after non-delivery, while the present dispute involves delayed completion and an attempted cure. The analysis extracts the rule on repudiation, compares the timing and seriousness of the conduct, and explains whether the factual differences matter.

template_name: Agreement Identity and Legal Characterization
description: Determines which alleged agreement or transaction structure governs when the same payment, conduct, or relationship is characterized in competing ways.
application_scenario: Use when one side describes a transaction as a loan, deposit, sale, partnership, employment, tenancy, guarantee, or other arrangement while the other side attributes it to a different agreement or legal relationship.
reasoning_flow: List each alleged agreement or legal relationship separately.
Identify the parties, subject matter, consideration, obligations, and intended commercial purpose associated with each version.
Map payments, documents, communications, and conduct to the agreement they most naturally concern.
Check whether the competing versions can coexist or whether they are mutually inconsistent.
Assess which characterization best accounts for the full course of dealing without leaving material conduct unexplained.
Use the selected characterization as the basis for analyzing obligations, breach, and remedies.
example_application: A payment is described by one party as an advance for goods and by the other as a contribution to a joint venture. The template separates the two proposed arrangements, maps invoices, profit-sharing conduct, and repayment demands to each, and identifies the characterization that best fits the transaction as a whole.

template_name: Formation and Assent Inferred from Conduct
description: Assesses whether an agreement or contractual term was accepted through words and conduct even though no single fully executed document conclusively records assent.
application_scenario: Use when the alleged contract is oral, unsigned, partly documented, incorporated through correspondence, or performed before formal execution.
reasoning_flow: Identify the proposed terms and the communication in which they were presented.
Separate conduct that merely continues negotiations from conduct that objectively implements the proposed terms.
Examine payments, performance, references to document numbers, use of contractual procedures, and acceptance of benefits.
Check whether later documents confirm, supplement, or contradict the alleged agreement.
Assess whether the parties' conduct demonstrates mutual assent to the relevant terms.
Define the resulting agreement narrowly so that only terms objectively accepted are carried forward.
example_application: A contractor never signs a standard-form contract but performs the work, uses its reference number, follows its payment mechanism, and later enters a supplemental arrangement tied to it. The template tests whether that conduct objectively manifests assent to the relevant standard terms.

template_name: Contractual Term Scope and Construction
description: Determines the meaning and reach of a disputed contractual clause by reading the text together with the agreement's structure, commercial purpose, and admissible contextual evidence.
application_scenario: Use when the dispute concerns whether a clause applies to particular transactions, periods, payments, termination steps, delivery obligations, or categories of performance.
reasoning_flow: State the competing interpretations of the disputed term.
Read the clause in its immediate textual setting and in the agreement as a whole.
Identify defined terms, conditions, exceptions, temporal limits, and cross-references that affect scope.
Compare each interpretation with the agreement's commercial purpose and the parties' documented implementation.
Distinguish evidence of the original meaning from evidence of a later change.
Apply the interpretation that gives coherent effect to the contractual scheme and the relevant language.
example_application: An employee claims that a bonus clause covers later transactions, while the employer reads the clause as limited to a narrower period and business segment. The template compares the clause, related provisions, and contemporaneous implementation before fixing its scope.

template_name: Oral Agreement or Informal Variation Verification
description: Evaluates an alleged oral agreement or informal variation by requiring a precise account of its terms and testing that account against subsequent conduct and contemporaneous records.
application_scenario: Use when a party alleges that an existing arrangement was created, replaced, extended, or modified orally or through an informal note.
reasoning_flow: Identify the alleged time, participants, subject matter, consideration, and essential terms of the oral or informal arrangement.
Determine which party bears the burden of establishing the arrangement or variation.
Compare the allegation with contemporaneous notes, receipts, correspondence, payments, and later statements.
Identify acts that are specifically referable to the alleged arrangement rather than equally consistent with the prior relationship.
Test whether the alleged change complies with any writing, formality, or no-oral-modification requirement.
Carry forward only the terms established with sufficient precision and evidential reliability.
example_application: A party says that a written compensation scheme was later narrowed by an oral discussion recorded in a handwritten note. The template tests the precision of the alleged change, the note's provenance, later payment behavior, and any contractual formality requirement.

template_name: Obligation–Performance–Breach Mapping
description: Converts a contract dispute into a structured comparison between each operative obligation, the required time or condition for performance, the conduct actually proved, and any asserted excuse.
application_scenario: Use in claims involving non-payment, non-completion, late delivery, defective work, failure to transfer property, failure to close an account, or failure to perform a promised service.
reasoning_flow: Extract each material obligation from the governing agreement.
Record the party responsible, required act, timing, conditions precedent, and contractual standard for each obligation.
Map the proved acts and omissions to the corresponding obligation.
Separate complete performance, partial performance, delayed performance, and non-performance.
Evaluate any contractual excuse, waiver, prevention, set-off, or external impediment linked to the obligation.
Identify the breach findings that remain after accounting for valid excuses and reciprocal obligations.
example_application: A seller claims an unpaid balance, while the buyer alleges late delivery and extra shipping costs. The template maps quantity, delivery timing, payment terms, notice of production problems, and claimed expenses to the corresponding obligations before any loss analysis.

template_name: Burden-Aligned Evidence Matrix
description: Organizes proof issue by issue and element by element so that evidence is evaluated against the proposition and burden it must satisfy rather than as an undifferentiated factual narrative.
application_scenario: Use whenever liability depends on disputed formation, performance, payment, title, authority, notice, causation, or another proposition requiring proof.
reasoning_flow: Break each legal issue into the factual and legal propositions that must be established.
Assign the burden and applicable standard of proof for each proposition.
Classify each item of evidence as direct, circumstantial, documentary, testimonial, expert, or admitted.
Place evidence under the proposition it bears on and note any material contradiction.
Identify gaps where the burden-bearing party lacks evidence on an essential proposition.
Reach a proposition-specific finding before combining the findings into the broader issue analysis.
example_application: A purchaser challenges title because identity details differ across instruments. The template isolates identity, execution, authority, and continuity of ownership, assigns the burden for each proposition, and evaluates identity documents, attestations, signatures, and declarations under the relevant proposition.

template_name: Credibility, Corroboration, and Evidential Gaps
description: Assesses conflicting accounts by comparing internal consistency, contemporaneous records, independent corroboration, conduct, and unexplained evidential omissions.
application_scenario: Use when the dispute turns materially on oral testimony, authenticity, agency, payment, informal notice, or the existence of an unwritten arrangement.
reasoning_flow: Identify the material factual conflicts between the competing accounts.
Check each account for internal consistency and consistency with earlier statements.
Compare testimony with contemporaneous documents and objectively verifiable conduct.
Give distinct weight to independent witnesses and records created before litigation.
Identify missing witnesses, absent records, or unexplained failures to produce evidence within a party's control.
Assess whether the evidential gaps weaken a proposition, while avoiding automatic conclusions from absence alone.
example_application: One party relies on an alleged payment and disputed receipt, while the other denies both. The template compares the receipt with admitted signatures, surrounding rent records, witness accounts, later conduct, and any unexplained absence of the person who handled the transaction.

template_name: Defense and Counterclaim Element Testing
description: Tests a defense or counterclaim as an independent set of propositions rather than treating it as established merely because it responds to the primary claim.
application_scenario: Use when a party relies on defective performance, late delivery, reduced rent, set-off, waiver, permission, collateral agreement, or another affirmative answer to a contract claim.
reasoning_flow: State the defense or counterclaim independently from the primary claim.
Identify its legal basis and required factual elements.
Assign the burden for each affirmative proposition.
Map the evidence to breach, causation, notice, quantification, and any required contractual procedure.
Check whether the asserted defense is consistent with the party's payments, correspondence, and prior conduct.
Determine the extent to which the established defense changes liability, quantum, or the available remedy.
example_application: A tenant admits paying less than the stated rent but attributes the reduction to serious interference with use of the premises. The template separately tests the landlord's obligations, the interference, notice, causation, and the relationship between the proven interference and the withheld sum.

template_name: Causation, Foreseeability, and Loss Attribution
description: Links each claimed item of loss to the established breach and separates ordinary contractual consequences from losses caused by independent events, the claimant's own conduct, or undisclosed special circumstances.
application_scenario: Use when a party claims resale loss, wasted expenditure, financing costs, shipping expenses, repair costs, lost remuneration, or other consequential loss.
reasoning_flow: List each claimed loss item separately.
Identify the breach alleged to have caused each item.
Construct the factual sequence from breach to loss and identify intervening events.
Assess whether the type of loss ordinarily follows from the breach or depended on special circumstances communicated at contracting.
Separate loss attributable to the breach from loss attributable to market movement, third parties, regulatory non-compliance, or the claimant's own decisions.
Carry forward only loss items with an adequately proved causal and foreseeable connection.
example_application: A buyer seeks emergency freight costs after alleged late delivery, but the seller may not have known the buyer's downstream deadline. The template tests the delivery obligation, communicated urgency, actual cause of the freight expense, and whether the claimed loss was within the parties' reasonable contemplation.

template_name: Mitigation and Reasonable Post-Breach Response
description: Evaluates whether the claimant took reasonable post-breach steps to limit loss without imposing hindsight perfection or requiring measures that were unavailable on the information then known.
application_scenario: Use when damages depend on resale, replacement performance, repair, price adjustment, account closure, or another response taken after breach.
reasoning_flow: Identify when the claimant knew or should have known that mitigating action was required.
Describe the practical options reasonably available at that time.
Assess the information, advice, market conditions, time pressure, and transaction costs known to the claimant.
Compare the chosen response with reasonable alternatives without using later events as automatic proof of unreasonableness.
Determine whether any avoidable increment of loss was caused by an unreasonable omission or choice.
Adjust the recoverable loss only to the extent that avoidable loss is proved.
example_application: After a failed property transaction, the seller markets the asset at an initial asking price above a later valuation and reduces the price as the market deteriorates. The template evaluates the information and professional advice available at each stage rather than judging the initial decision solely from the eventual resale price.

template_name: Substantial-Dispute Threshold for Debt-Based Proceedings
description: Determines whether a debt-based insolvency or comparable summary procedure may proceed by testing whether the asserted dispute has a genuine evidential and legal foundation rather than merely being asserted.
application_scenario: Use when a winding-up, bankruptcy, statutory-demand, or adjournment application depends on whether the underlying contractual debt is genuinely disputed or realistically payable within a short period.
reasoning_flow: Identify the precise debt, contractual source, due date, and demand relied upon.
Separate disputes about liability, amount, set-off, contractual entitlement, and procedural defects.
Require the resisting party to articulate a coherent factual and legal basis for each dispute.
Compare that basis with acknowledgments, payment history, contemporaneous documents, and contractual integration or amendment clauses.
Distinguish a substantial dispute from a bare assertion, speculative future recovery, or unsubstantiated repayment assurance.
Apply the procedural threshold without conducting a full trial of genuinely triable contractual issues.
example_application: A company facing a debt-based petition says that a documented loan was actually part of a wider acquisition arrangement and also points to an expected receivable. The template tests the contractual documents, prior acknowledgments, payment conduct, and evidence of near-term liquidity at the threshold level.

template_name: Contract Remedy and Quantum Construction
description: Builds the remedy from established liability and proved financial consequences, while preventing double counting and separating contractual, restitutionary, possessory, and discretionary components.
application_scenario: Use after liability analysis in claims for damages, debt, arrears, deposit return, compensation, maintenance, possession, or other quantified relief.
reasoning_flow: Identify the legal basis and objective of each requested remedy.
Fix the relevant valuation or accounting period and the contractual baseline.
Calculate principal loss, unpaid sums, credits, deposits, part payments, and proven incidental expenses separately.
Remove amounts already compensated, contractually excluded, too remote, unproved, or attributable to another cause.
Check whether interest, possession, rescission, forfeiture, restitution, or discretionary adjustment requires a distinct legal basis.
Present a transparent calculation showing how each allowed component contributes to the remedy.
example_application: A claimant seeks an unpaid contractual balance plus expenses, while the other party has made part payments and asserts offsets. The template establishes the contractual baseline, credits all proven payments, tests each expense and offset separately, and produces an auditable net calculation.

template_name: Multi-Source Rule Synthesis
description: Construct a single operational legal test from statutes, regulations, common-law principles, and cited authorities that address the same issue.
application_scenario: Use when the case materials provide several legal sources and the decision-maker must determine how they combine, qualify, or supplement one another.
reasoning_flow: Identify each source that governs the issue and classify it as statutory text, regulatory rule, common-law principle, or precedent.
Extract the operative requirement, exception, burden, and remedial consequence from each source.
Resolve overlap by giving controlling sources priority and treating other authorities as interpretation, refinement, or illustration.
Express the combined rule as a sequence of elements that can be matched to the facts.
Record any unresolved conflict or gap that requires a narrower fallback rule.
example_application: A claimant invokes a safety ordinance, a related regulation, and prior negligence decisions. The analysis converts them into one test covering the protected class, required precaution, breach, causation, and available damages.

template_name: Material-Fact Precedent Analogy
description: Determine whether a precedent's rule extends to the present dispute by comparing legally material facts rather than surface similarities.
application_scenario: Use when a prior decision or formula is invoked and its applicability depends on factual similarity, the purpose of the rule, or the presence of an exception.
reasoning_flow: State the precise proposition for which the earlier authority is being used.
Identify the facts that were material to that proposition in the earlier authority.
Identify the corresponding facts in the present dispute and separate similarities from legally meaningful differences.
Test whether the policy or rationale of the earlier rule remains engaged despite the differences.
Apply the precedent, limit it, or distinguish it only to the extent justified by the material-fact comparison.
example_application: A party relies on an earlier damages formula. The analysis compares the type of loss, evidentiary basis, and statutory setting before deciding whether the formula can be used unchanged or requires adaptation.

template_name: Negligence Element Mapping
description: Organize a negligence claim into duty, standard of care, breach, factual and legal causation, and legally recoverable damage.
application_scenario: Use in personal injury, workplace, occupiers' liability, traffic, property damage, or management-failure disputes framed in negligence.
reasoning_flow: Identify the relationship and circumstances alleged to create a duty of care.
Define the applicable standard by reference to foreseeable risk, reasonable precautions, professional practice, or governing legislation.
Match the alleged acts and omissions to the standard and identify the specific breach theory.
Test factual causation and then consider remoteness, intervening events, and the scope of the risk.
Separate liability findings from the later assessment of each recoverable head of damage.
example_application: An occupier knew of a hazardous condition and had adopted safety instructions. The analysis examines whether the precautions were reasonable, whether they were implemented, and whether the hazard caused the claimant's injury.

template_name: Statutory Duty as Standard of Care
description: Use a statutory or regulatory obligation to define or inform the conduct required in a related negligence claim.
application_scenario: Use when an accident occurs in a regulated setting and the claimant relies on both a legislative safety requirement and common-law negligence.
reasoning_flow: Identify the person or entity on whom the legislation places the obligation.
Determine the class of persons and type of harm the provision is designed to protect.
Translate the legislative command into the concrete precaution required in the circumstances.
Compare the defendant's conduct with that precaution and determine whether any permitted qualification applies.
Assess whether the statutory departure is causally connected to the injury and how it interacts with the common-law claim.
example_application: A workplace rule requires effective measures against objects falling from equipment. The analysis identifies the responsible contractor, the required safeguard, the exposed workers, and the causal link between the missing safeguard and the accident.

template_name: Contributory Negligence and Fault Apportionment
description: Evaluate whether the claimant failed to take reasonable care for personal safety and, if so, allocate responsibility according to causal potency and blameworthiness.
application_scenario: Use when both the defendant's negligence and the claimant's conduct may have contributed to an accident or aggravated the resulting loss.
reasoning_flow: Identify the precautions reasonably expected from the claimant in the actual circumstances.
Determine whether the claimant knew or should have known of the relevant danger.
Compare the claimant's conduct with ordinary practice, instructions, signals, and the time available to react.
Assess the causal contribution of each party's conduct rather than treating every careless act as equally significant.
Allocate responsibility by weighing both causal potency and relative blameworthiness, then apply the resulting proportion to divisible damages.
example_application: A road user follows one traffic signal while another road user proceeds despite an obstructed view. The analysis compares each person's opportunity to perceive and avoid the danger before apportioning responsibility.

template_name: Medical Causation with Pre-Existing Vulnerability
description: Separate accident-caused injury from pre-existing vulnerability while preserving liability for harm that the accident materially caused or accelerated.
application_scenario: Use when medical evidence indicates that a claimant had an earlier condition, degeneration, disability, or susceptibility relevant to the present symptoms.
reasoning_flow: Establish the claimant's condition and functional level before the accident.
Identify the new pathology, symptoms, or deterioration appearing after the accident.
Determine whether the accident caused, aggravated, accelerated, or merely coincided with the condition.
Distinguish indivisible harm from components that can be medically separated by cause or time.
Adjust the damages period or amount only where the evidence permits a reasoned allocation to the pre-existing condition.
example_application: A claimant had asymptomatic degeneration before an accident and later developed disabling symptoms. The analysis compares baseline function, medical opinions, and the natural progression of the condition to isolate the accident-related loss.

template_name: Head-by-Head Damages Assessment
description: Assess compensation separately for each legally recognized head of loss before combining the amounts and applying adjustments.
application_scenario: Use in personal injury, fatal accident, property damage, or other compensation claims involving multiple categories of past and future loss.
reasoning_flow: List each claimed head of loss and classify it as non-pecuniary, past pecuniary, future pecuniary, or expense-based.
For each head, identify the governing measure, required proof, and relevant period.
Exclude duplication where the same consequence is captured by more than one head.
Calculate each proven head independently using the best available evidence and any accepted benchmark.
Combine the heads only after applying issue-specific contingencies, deductions, and interest rules.
example_application: A serious injury claim includes pain and loss of amenities, treatment expenses, past wage loss, future wage loss, and care costs. The analysis values each category separately and checks for overlap before aggregation.

template_name: Earnings and Earning-Capacity Projection
description: Estimate past and future income loss by comparing the claimant's probable but-for earnings with residual earning ability after the injury.
application_scenario: Use when injury affects employment, career progression, working hours, occupational options, or competitiveness in the labor market.
reasoning_flow: Establish the pre-incident earnings baseline from reliable employment, tax, business, or market evidence.
Determine the periods of complete incapacity, partial incapacity, and return to work.
Estimate residual earning ability by considering functional limits, qualifications, actual post-incident work, and realistic alternatives.
Project the but-for and residual earnings streams over an appropriate working period.
Apply contingencies for uncertain career progression, unemployment, health, and other ordinary vicissitudes without duplicating a separate earning-capacity award.
example_application: An injured worker returns to lower-paid casual work but retains some occupational ability. The analysis compares the likely pre-injury career path with realistic post-injury options and separates accrued loss from future loss.

template_name: Multiplier-Multiplicand Loss Calculation
description: Calculate a continuing future loss by pairing an annual or periodic net loss with a multiplier that reflects duration, acceleration, and contingencies.
application_scenario: Use for dependency claims, future earnings, recurring care costs, or other losses expected to continue over time.
reasoning_flow: Define the multiplicand as the net annual or periodic loss after personal expenditure, taxes, benefits, or residual earnings where relevant.
Identify the expected duration of the loss by reference to age, working life, dependency, treatment, or care needs.
Select a multiplier that accounts for accelerated receipt and ordinary contingencies.
Check that the multiplier does not duplicate contingencies already built into the multiplicand.
Perform sensitivity checks where either the duration or the periodic amount is materially uncertain.
example_application: A dependent loses regular household financial contributions. The analysis derives a net annual dependency figure, estimates the likely duration of contribution, and applies a contingency-adjusted multiplier.

template_name: Medical Evidence and Prognosis Reconciliation
description: Reconcile medical opinions and translate diagnosis, impairment, treatment, and prognosis into legally relevant findings on causation and loss.
application_scenario: Use when several clinicians, treatment records, or impairment assessments address the claimant's present condition and future recovery.
reasoning_flow: Separate objective findings, reported symptoms, diagnoses, treatment history, and functional observations.
Compare experts on the factual assumptions, examination dates, specialties, and methods underlying their opinions.
Resolve apparent disagreement by identifying whether the experts address different conditions, periods, or legal questions.
Determine the most reliable prognosis, including likely improvement, deterioration, treatment, and residual disability.
Translate the reconciled medical findings into the relevant damages periods and functional restrictions.
example_application: Different doctors agree on the injury but differ on future improvement and treatment. The analysis identifies the basis of each opinion and converts the most reliable prognosis into work, care, and non-pecuniary loss assumptions.

template_name: Damages Adjustments and Anti-Duplication
description: Apply post-calculation adjustments while preserving full compensation and preventing duplication or legally impermissible deductions.
application_scenario: Use after the primary heads of damage have been calculated and questions arise about improvement of property, insurance or compensation payments, prior awards, contingencies, or interest.
reasoning_flow: Identify every proposed addition or deduction and the legal rule governing it.
Determine whether a payment or benefit is collateral, compensatory for the same loss, or recoverable under a separate statutory scheme.
Check whether repair or replacement produces unavoidable betterment and whether the law permits a reduction for it.
Remove overlap between damages heads and prior compensation without reducing recovery for distinct losses.
Calculate interest separately for the categories and periods to which the applicable rule assigns it.
example_application: A claimant seeks repair costs and has also received a payment from another source. The analysis classifies the payment, tests whether the repair improvement is unavoidable, checks for double recovery, and then computes any interest.

template_name: Interim Discretionary Relief Assessment
description: Evaluate an interim or restorative remedy through a staged inquiry into threshold merits, necessity, practical consequences, and equitable discretion.
application_scenario: Use for provisional appointments, mandatory injunctions, restoration orders, or comparable remedies sought before final resolution or requiring discretionary intervention.
reasoning_flow: Confirm jurisdiction, standing, and the legal power to grant the requested form of relief.
Assess whether the applicant has shown a sufficiently arguable underlying right or claim.
Identify urgency, risk of irreparable or uncompensable harm, asset dissipation, management failure, or other need for immediate intervention.
Compare the practical consequences of granting and withholding relief, including workable alternatives.
Consider delay, applicant conduct, third-party effects, public interest, and whether tailored conditions can reduce prejudice.
example_application: An applicant seeks immediate control measures while the underlying dispute remains unresolved. The analysis tests the arguable claim, the risk of deterioration without intervention, available alternatives, and the comparative impact on affected parties.

template_name: Separate Primary Claim, Defense, and Counterclaim
description: Decompose a dispute into the claimant's affirmative basis for relief, each defense that would defeat or reduce that basis, and any counterclaim seeking independent relief. Keep these tracks distinct before considering their interaction.
application_scenario: Use when pleadings combine a payment, possession, performance, or damages claim with one or more defenses, set-offs, or counterclaims.
reasoning_flow: State the primary claim and identify the legal elements the claimant must establish.
List each defense and identify the element or remedy it is directed against.
Identify any counterclaim that can stand independently of the defense.
Assign the applicable burden for each claim, defense, and counterclaim.
Resolve each track separately before determining how they affect the net relief.
example_application: A contractor seeks a final payment, while the customer alleges defective work and claims the cost of corrective work. Analyze the payment claim, the defect defense, and the corrective-cost counterclaim as separate tracks before calculating any net amount.

template_name: Identify the Controlling Legal Relationship and Instrument
description: Determine which legal relationship and instrument actually generate the asserted right or obligation before testing performance or defenses. Distinguish related but legally separate sources such as a contract, settlement, credit instrument, tenancy, mortgage, or statutory right.
application_scenario: Use when the same facts can be characterized under multiple agreements, instruments, or legal regimes, or when the defense depends on selecting the correct source of obligation.
reasoning_flow: List the plausible legal relationships and instruments raised by the facts.
Match each requested remedy to the source that could authorize it.
Identify the operative terms, statutory provisions, or doctrines for each source.
Separate obligations that are independent from obligations that are merely connected factually.
Proceed under the source that directly governs the disputed obligation while preserving any alternative basis.
example_application: A seller seeks payment after documents were presented under a financing instrument, while the buyer raises defects under the sale contract. Determine whether the immediate claim arises from the financing instrument, the sale contract, or both, and analyze each obligation under its own rules.

template_name: Test Formation, Variation, Renewal, or Settlement Enforceability
description: Assess whether an alleged agreement or later modification created enforceable obligations by examining assent, certainty, authority, consideration or equivalent formal requirements, and objective conduct.
application_scenario: Use when a party relies on an alleged oral agreement, renewed lease, annual supply arrangement, amended term, development arrangement, or settlement record.
reasoning_flow: Identify the precise agreement, variation, renewal, or settlement alleged.
Extract the essential terms said to have been agreed.
Evaluate objective evidence of offer, acceptance, authority, and intention to be bound.
Check whether required formalities or conditions precedent were satisfied.
Distinguish negotiation, provisional arrangement, and completed agreement.
Define the obligations that arise only if enforceability is established.
example_application: An occupier says the owner agreed to a new tenancy after the original term, while the owner says negotiations never became final. Examine the alleged terms, communications, authority, formal requirements, and subsequent conduct before treating the renewal as binding.

template_name: Map Obligations, Conditions, and Performance Chronology
description: Convert a lengthy factual record into an ordered map of contractual duties, triggering conditions, deadlines, acts of performance, and alleged failures. This creates the factual foundation for later breach and defense analysis.
application_scenario: Use in fact-heavy disputes involving staged work, delivery schedules, payment milestones, notices, possession, title documents, or sequential contractual obligations.
reasoning_flow: Identify each material obligation and the party responsible for it.
Record any condition precedent, notice requirement, deadline, or dependency attached to the obligation.
Place the relevant acts and omissions in chronological order.
Exclude facts that do not affect formation, performance, breach, causation, defense, or remedy.
Mark factual conflicts and missing information at the point where they affect the sequence.
Use the completed map to identify which obligation became due and whether it was performed.
example_application: A project requires completion of work, certification, invoicing, and final payment in sequence. Build a timeline showing when each step was due, what occurred, and whether an earlier unmet condition prevented a later payment obligation from arising.

template_name: Determine Breach, Repudiation, and Termination Rights
description: Evaluate whether non-performance, defective performance, delay, or an announced refusal amounts to breach and whether it gives the other party a right to suspend, terminate, or claim contractual relief.
application_scenario: Use for disputes over late delivery, refusal to supply, defective work, non-payment, failure to complete, or purported termination.
reasoning_flow: Identify the obligation allegedly breached and classify the relevant term or duty.
Determine the required standard, quantity, quality, timing, or manner of performance.
Compare the required performance with the proven act, omission, or statement.
Assess whether the breach is actual, anticipatory, material, or remediable.
Check notice, cure, waiver, affirmation, and termination requirements.
Identify the remedies or continuing obligations that follow from the breach classification.
example_application: A manufacturer misses delivery dates and the buyer cancels the remaining orders. Determine whether time was contractually critical, whether the delay was material, whether any cure or notice was required, and whether cancellation was authorized.

template_name: Evaluate Excuse, Suspension, and Avoidance Defenses
description: Test a defense that performance or enforcement is excused, suspended, redirected, or barred by a contractual clause, supervening event, representation, statute, or agreed dispute process.
application_scenario: Use when a party invokes impossibility, frustration, estoppel, a rent or payment suspension clause, a statutory safe harbor, arbitration, waiver, or another avoidance doctrine.
reasoning_flow: Identify the exact defense and the obligation or remedy it targets.
State the elements and threshold conditions of the defense.
Match the material facts to each element without assuming the defense applies merely because hardship or non-performance occurred.
Check contractual allocation of the relevant risk and any exclusion or preservation clause.
Assess causation, notice, reliance, mitigation, and consistency of later conduct where relevant.
Determine the scope of the defense, including whether it defeats, delays, narrows, or redirects the claim.
example_application: A party stops payment after an external event delays a project and relies on a clause addressing unforeseen circumstances. Compare the event and its consequences with the clause and the governing doctrine to determine whether performance was excused, merely postponed, or still required.

template_name: Assess Set-Off and Cross-Obligation Defenses
description: Determine whether an asserted cross-obligation may reduce or answer the primary claim, especially where the debts arise from separate transactions, accounts, contracts, or parties.
application_scenario: Use in debt, banking, construction, settlement, and commercial disputes where a party seeks to deduct another alleged liability from the amount claimed.
reasoning_flow: Identify the primary debt and the alleged cross-obligation.
Confirm the parties, capacities, maturity, and legal character of both obligations.
Determine whether the governing contract, statute, procedure, or equitable doctrine permits set-off.
Check whether the cross-obligation is sufficiently connected, liquidated, due, and enforceable.
Distinguish a true set-off from a separate counterclaim or accounting exercise.
Calculate the net position only after both obligations have been independently established.
example_application: A purchaser admits an invoice balance but alleges costs under another project. Test mutuality, connection, maturity, and any contractual restriction before treating those costs as a deduction rather than a separate counterclaim.

template_name: Resolve Material Factual Conflicts by Issue
description: Organize competing factual accounts around the legal issue they affect, prioritize contemporaneous and objective evidence, and avoid treating every inconsistency as outcome-determinative.
application_scenario: Use when parties dispute whether an agreement was made, notice was given, performance occurred, premises were defective, documents conformed, or a representation induced reliance.
reasoning_flow: Identify the disputed factual proposition and the legal element it affects.
Collect the evidence for each competing account.
Compare contemporaneous documents, conduct, inherent probability, and witness reliability.
Separate direct contradiction from ambiguity, omission, or immaterial inconsistency.
State which facts remain uncertain and whether the burden of proof resolves that uncertainty.
Carry only the material factual findings into the next legal template.
example_application: One party says a supply commitment covered the full year, while the other says orders were accepted only individually. Compare the written instruments, correspondence, ordering pattern, and later conduct to resolve the factual premise needed for contract interpretation.

template_name: Interpret Contract Terms and Allocate Transactional Risk
description: Interpret disputed language in the contract as a whole and determine how the agreement allocates risks such as delay, defects, external events, payment interruption, title problems, or document discrepancies.
application_scenario: Use when liability turns on the meaning or scope of a clause rather than solely on whether an event occurred.
reasoning_flow: Identify the disputed words and the competing interpretations.
Read the clause with related provisions and the structure of the agreement.
Consider the objective commercial purpose and factual matrix permitted by the governing law.
Check definitions, exceptions, conditions, notice provisions, and conflict clauses.
Avoid an interpretation that makes related provisions redundant or commercially incoherent unless the language requires it.
Translate the preferred interpretation into concrete rights, duties, and allocated risks.
example_application: A tenant relies on a clause said to suspend rent when premises cannot be fully used. Interpret the trigger, duration, exceptions, and related repair provisions to determine what risk the clause assigns to each party.

template_name: Select Remedy and Measure Monetary Consequences
description: After establishing the relevant right and any defense, select the legally available remedy and calculate its scope without double recovery. Distinguish expectation, reliance, restitutionary, possessory, declaratory, accounting, and equitable relief.
application_scenario: Use when a dispute seeks payment, refund, damages, possession, mesne profits, an account, return of property, declaration, or specific performance.
reasoning_flow: Link each requested remedy to an established cause of action or equitable basis.
Identify the governing measure and valuation date for monetary relief.
Separate principal loss, consequential loss, interest, use value, and recoverable expenses.
Apply causation, remoteness, mitigation, credit, forfeiture, and duplication constraints.
Check whether non-monetary or equitable relief requires inadequacy of damages, clean hands, readiness, or judicial discretion.
Present alternative calculations where liability or valuation depends on unresolved findings.
example_application: A buyer seeks return of a deposit and additional losses after a failed property transaction. Identify the legal basis for restitution and damages, credit any retained benefit, apply the proper valuation point, and avoid counting the same loss twice.

template_name: Test Necessity and Proportionality of Interim or Procedural Relief
description: Evaluate whether an interlocutory or procedural order is authorized, necessary to protect the dispute, and proportionate to its burden, while keeping the merits separate from provisional case management.
application_scenario: Use for requests involving preservation of property, payment into court, interim payment, disclosure of valuation material, additional pleadings, default procedures, stays, or costs.
reasoning_flow: Identify the procedural power invoked and its threshold requirements.
Specify the practical risk or case-management need the order is meant to address.
Assess the apparent strength of the underlying claim only to the degree permitted at the interim stage.
Compare the likely benefit of the order with delay, expense, prejudice, and availability of narrower measures.
Consider undertakings, safeguards, security, and reversibility.
Define the order's scope without finally deciding disputed substantive rights.
example_application: A party asks the court to preserve disputed goods pending an accounting claim. Determine whether there is a real preservation risk, whether the property is sufficiently identified, and whether a narrower safeguard would protect both sides.

template_name: Procedural Gateway Before Merits
description: Determines whether the court or tribunal may entertain a claim, appeal, or application before addressing the underlying substantive dispute.
application_scenario: Use when the requested relief depends on jurisdiction, leave, standing, valid commencement, a statutory precondition, or another gateway requirement.
reasoning_flow: Identify the precise order sought and the legal source said to authorize it.
Extract each mandatory gateway condition and distinguish jurisdictional requirements from matters of discretion.
Map the material facts to each condition, including filing posture, party status, territorial or subject-matter connection, and any required prior step.
Identify missing proof, disputed gateway facts, and any irregularity that may be cured or waived.
Proceed to the substantive issues only after recording whether the procedural gateway is available.
example_application: A party seeks ancillary property relief, but the court must first examine the required connection to the forum and whether leave is available before considering ownership or valuation questions.

template_name: Substantive Right Before Interim Protection
description: Separates the arguable underlying right from the additional considerations governing temporary protective relief.
application_scenario: Use for interlocutory injunctions, receivership, preservation orders, or comparable temporary measures sought before final determination.
reasoning_flow: Identify the substantive right or interest that the applicant says requires protection.
Assess whether the claim raises a genuine issue fit for determination without deciding the final merits.
Identify the threatened change, dissipation, interference, or practical harm that may occur before trial.
Compare the adequacy of damages and the relative prejudice created by granting or withholding temporary relief.
Select a proportionate measure directed to preserving the relevant property, assets, evidence, or existing position.
example_application: A claimant asserting a beneficial interest in premises seeks to prevent transfer or alteration while the ownership dispute remains unresolved.

template_name: Competing Title, Beneficial Interest, and Possession
description: Analyzes competing claims based on legal title, beneficial ownership, trust or nominee arrangements, and factual possession without treating those concepts as interchangeable.
application_scenario: Use when one party relies on registered or documentary title while another relies on contribution, intention, family or business arrangements, exclusive control, or long possession.
reasoning_flow: Identify the property or interest in dispute and the formal title position.
State each alternative basis of entitlement, such as beneficial ownership, resulting or constructive trust, nominee status, customary interest, easement, or adverse possession.
Trace the evidence of acquisition, payment, intention, control, occupation, exclusion, acknowledgment, and dealings with third parties.
Allocate the burden of proof for each asserted basis and test whether the evidence satisfies its distinct elements.
Keep any declaration, possession order, vesting order, or protective remedy tied to the interest actually established.
example_application: The registered owner disputes a claim by an occupier who relies on exclusive control and an alleged understanding that title was held for another person.

template_name: Statutory Classification of Property or Use
description: Determines whether land, structures, premises, activities, or uses fall within a statutory definition that triggers a regulatory consequence.
application_scenario: Use when the dispute turns on labels such as building, building works, agricultural land, pond, premises, tenancy category, or another defined property-related term.
reasoning_flow: Extract the operative definition together with any inclusions, exclusions, deeming provisions, and linked terms.
Identify the ordinary, technical, and statutory meanings that are reasonably available in context.
Separate physical characteristics from functional use, legal designation, and temporary or artificial features.
Compare the facts with the purpose and structure of the statutory scheme and with materially similar authorities.
Apply the selected interpretation consistently to the relevant property, structure, or activity.
example_application: A regulatory exemption depends on whether a water-based installation is legally classified by its physical form, its commercial function, or the kind of activity carried on there.

template_name: Service, Notice, and Fair Opportunity to Respond
description: Tests whether affected persons received the process, notice, and opportunity to respond required before an order or administrative decision was made.
application_scenario: Use for disputed service, inadequate notice periods, ex parte applications, default orders, absent parties, or failures to disclose the case to be answered.
reasoning_flow: Identify the procedural step requiring service, notice, disclosure, or an opportunity to be heard.
Determine the prescribed method, recipient, timing, and content of the required communication.
Compare formal compliance with evidence of actual knowledge and any conduct showing deliberate avoidance or genuine lack of awareness.
Assess whether the defect caused practical prejudice and whether it can be cured by directions, adjournment, re-service, or reopening.
Relate the defect to the validity of the existing order or decision and to the scope of any corrective relief.
example_application: A person asks to reopen proceedings after learning of an order made in their absence, requiring examination of service records, actual awareness, delay, and resulting prejudice.

template_name: Temporal Law and Accrued Rights Check
description: Determines which version of a legal regime governs when the relevant acts, application, decision, or claimed rights span a legislative change.
application_scenario: Use when a statute is amended or repealed after a notice, application, transaction, or enforcement step but before final determination.
reasoning_flow: Construct a chronology of the legally significant acts and the commencement of the old and new regimes.
Identify any express transitional, savings, retrospective, or pending-proceeding provisions.
Distinguish a completed or accrued right from a mere expectation, procedure, or continuing application.
Determine which law governs each separate step rather than assuming one version governs the entire dispute.
Check whether the decision-maker relied on a later rule in a manner permitted by the transitional framework.
example_application: An application was lodged under an earlier regulatory scheme, and the decision-maker later applied amended criteria while the application remained undecided.

template_name: Appellate or Supervisory Error Classification
description: Classifies the alleged error and applies the review standard appropriate to an appeal, tribunal challenge, or judicial review.
application_scenario: Use when a party challenges a lower court, tribunal, or administrative decision rather than presenting the dispute at first instance.
reasoning_flow: Identify the decision under challenge, the available review route, and the scope of the reviewing body's powers.

Classify each complaint as jurisdictional error, legal misdirection, burden misallocation, evidential insufficiency, procedural unfairness, irrelevant consideration, unreasonableness, disproportionality, or discretionary error.
Separate reviewable error from disagreement about factual weight or preferred outcome.
Apply the standard of review and any deference appropriate to the decision-maker and issue type.
Match any corrective order to the identified error, including reconsideration, rehearing, variation, or setting aside.
example_application: A tribunal decision is challenged on the grounds that it assigned the burden incorrectly and failed to address a contractual exclusion relied on by one side.

template_name: Evidence and Burden at a Procedural Stage
description: Evaluates evidential sufficiency under the limited function of the current procedural stage rather than prematurely conducting a full trial.
