The court identifies which factors express the governing principle, compares the present investigation and stakeholder risks with the precedent, and explains why factual differences do or do not alter the analysis.

template_name: Element-by-Element Burden and Threshold Assessment
description: Structures an evidential assessment by assigning each disputed element to the party bearing the persuasive or evidential burden and testing the proof against the applicable threshold.
application_scenario: Use when liability or relief depends on several factual or legal elements, especially where the record contains admissions, conflicting accounts, or incomplete proof.
reasoning_flow: Break the issue into the legally material elements that must be established.
Identify which party bears the persuasive burden and whether any evidential burden may shift.
State the proof threshold applicable to each element or stage of the application.
Match admitted facts and reliable evidence to the elements they address.
Separate evidence that directly proves an element from evidence that only permits an inference.
Record counterevidence, unexplained gaps, and elements for which the burden remains unmet.
Combine the element findings without treating weakness on one element as proof of another.
example_application: A claimant alleges an unpaid obligation while the opposing party raises a distinct statutory defense. Assess the existence of the obligation, the amount remaining, and each defense element under its own burden and threshold.

template_name: Debt Existence and Outstanding Balance Reconciliation
description: Determines whether an enforceable payment obligation exists and calculates any remaining balance by reconstructing the underlying transactions and all recognized adjustments.
application_scenario: Use for disputed loans, unpaid goods, account deficits, dishonoured instruments, advances, or other claims in which both liability and the balance due are contested.
reasoning_flow: Identify the transaction said to create the payment obligation and the legal basis of the claim.
Separate principal, interest, fees, damages, and other components of the requested sum.
Map each advance, delivery, charge, or debit to contemporaneous records.
Credit admitted repayments, third-party payments, returns, rebates, set-offs, and agreed adjustments.
Reconcile inconsistencies among bank records, ledgers, invoices, receipts, and oral accounts.
Exclude components that lack a proved transactional basis or have already been discharged.
State the remaining components and balance that are established by the evidence.
example_application: A supplier claims an unpaid invoice balance, while the buyer relies on prior payments and debit adjustments. Reconstruct the deliveries and account entries, verify each adjustment, and calculate the residual obligation.

template_name: Characterization of a Disputed Transfer
description: Classifies a transfer of money or an instrument according to its proven legal and commercial purpose rather than the label later assigned by either side.
application_scenario: Use when the same transfer is described as a loan, purchase payment, trust money, gift, gratuitous payment, investment contribution, or security for another obligation.
reasoning_flow: List the competing characterizations and the legal consequences of each.
Identify who supplied the value, who received the practical benefit, and who controlled its use.
Examine contemporaneous requests, instructions, account entries, acknowledgments, and repayment terms.
Check whether interest, maturity, security, reporting, segregation, or return obligations were agreed or performed.
Compare later demands and conduct with the parties' behavior when the transfer occurred.
Assess whether the evidence establishes the essential features of one characterization more strongly than the alternatives.
Apply the resulting characterization to liability, repayment, ownership, or compensation.
example_application: One person transfers funds used in another person's business. One side later calls the transfer a personal loan, while the other calls it an investment or payment for goods. Determine the transfer's objective purpose from documents and conduct.

template_name: Conflicting Witness Account Credibility Assessment
description: Evaluates competing oral accounts through consistency, contemporaneous corroboration, plausibility, and witness conduct rather than demeanor alone.
application_scenario: Use when key facts depend on contradictory testimony about instructions, payments, ownership, repayment terms, settlement, or the purpose of a transaction.
reasoning_flow: Identify the precise factual propositions on which the witnesses disagree.
Compare each account with the witness's earlier statements, pleadings, correspondence, and recorded communications.
Test each account against objective records and undisputed surrounding events.
Check internal consistency, unexplained changes, omissions, and selective reconstruction.
Consider motive, interest, opportunity to observe, and the availability of corroborating witnesses.
Give greater weight to evidence that is independently corroborated and consistent with ordinary conduct.
Make only the factual findings necessary to resolve the disputed issues.
example_application: Two participants give incompatible versions of an oral instruction that determined when an account should be closed. Compare both versions with call records, margin notices, later conduct, and independent testimony.

template_name: Documentary Reliability, Completeness, and Weight
description: Assesses whether documents or recordings are authentic, complete, accurate, and sufficiently connected to the proposition for which they are offered.
application_scenario: Use when the dispute turns on ledgers, bank statements, invoices, reports, cheques, forms, emails, recordings, or other records whose accuracy or completeness is challenged.
reasoning_flow: Identify the proposition each document or recording is offered to prove.
Establish provenance, authorship, custody, and the method by which the record was created or preserved.
Check whether the record is complete for the relevant period and transaction.
Identify errors, alterations, missing segments, inconsistent entries, or unexplained metadata.
Cross-check the record against independent documents, admissions, and objectively verifiable events.
Distinguish an authentic record from an accurate or complete record.
Assign weight proportionate to the verified reliability and relevance of the material.
example_application: A party relies on transaction recordings and internal account statements, while the other alleges omissions. Verify how the records were produced, test them against external records, and limit their weight to what can be reliably established.

template_name: Missing Evidence and Evidential Gap Analysis
description: Determines the effect of absent records, witnesses, particulars, or verification without automatically treating absence as affirmative proof for the opposing position.
application_scenario: Use when a party fails to produce expected accounts, proof of payment, loss particulars, direct verification, a statement of affairs, or a witness with material knowledge.
reasoning_flow: Identify the element for which the missing material would be relevant.
Ask whether the material would ordinarily exist and whether it was reasonably available to the party expected to produce it.
Consider any explanation for non-production, loss, incompleteness, or inability to call the witness.
Determine whether the existing evidence can establish the element without the missing material.
Apply any legally permitted adverse inference only after checking control, relevance, and fairness.
Distinguish a failure to prove a proposition from proof that the opposite proposition is true.
State the limited evidential consequence of the gap for the affected element.
example_application: A creditor alleges a balance based on internal entries but produces no underlying invoices or proof of delivery. Determine whether the entries are independently corroborated and what follows from the missing source records.

template_name: Payment-Claim Defense and Counteradjustment Assessment
description: Tests whether a defense, set-off, counterclaim, or statutory objection defeats, reduces, or leaves unaffected an otherwise established payment claim.
application_scenario: Use when the responding party relies on defective performance, debit notes, prior settlement, excessive interest, illegality, authorization, payment, or another counteradjustment.
reasoning_flow: Classify each response as a denial, affirmative defense, set-off, counterclaim, discharge, or challenge to quantum.
Identify the elements and burden applicable to each response.
Separate defenses to the creation of liability from matters that only reduce the amount recoverable.
Test the asserted facts against contemporaneous complaints, notices, account records, and subsequent conduct.
Quantify any proved credit, loss, overpayment, or unenforceable component.
Determine whether any illegality or statutory consequence affects the whole transaction or only a severable part.
Apply each established defense or adjustment to the reconstructed claim.
example_application: A buyer admits receiving goods but alleges defects and relies on internal debit notes. Verify timely notice, proof of defect and loss, acceptance or continued use, and the amount of any valid reduction.

template_name: Statutory Status or Transaction Classification by Substance
description: Applies a statutory definition or legal category to the practical substance of a relationship or transaction using the relevant indicia as a whole.
application_scenario: Use when liability depends on whether facts amount to employment, a transfer of business, money-lending activity, insolvency, a regulated payment, or another defined status.
reasoning_flow: Extract the operative statutory definition, inclusions, exclusions, and legally recognized indicia.
Translate each criterion into factual questions that can be answered from the record.
Assess continuity, control, commercial purpose, risk, benefit, and surrounding conduct where relevant.
Treat contractual labels and self-serving descriptions as evidence but not as conclusive classifications.
Compare the whole factual pattern with the purpose and boundaries of the statutory category.
Address exceptions, deeming provisions, and consequences triggered by classification.
State the classification only to the extent needed for the linked liability or remedy issue.
example_application: A business closes and another operator continues from the same premises using similar assets, services, and permissions. Evaluate the continuity factors under the governing definition rather than relying only on the transaction's label.

template_name: Insolvency Debt, Dispute, and Payment-Capacity Assessment
description: Separates proof of the petition debt from any genuine dispute, payment event, or evidence concerning inability to pay, and then connects those findings to the insolvency procedure.
application_scenario: Use in winding-up, bankruptcy, annulment, or related proceedings where debt, solvency, payment, default, or the sufficiency of an asserted dispute is contested.
reasoning_flow: Verify the legal and evidential basis of the debt relied on for the insolvency process.
Reconcile the claimed debt with payments, credits, ledger entries, and third-party transactions.
Identify each ground on which the debt is disputed and the evidence supporting that ground.
Distinguish a genuine dispute grounded in substantial evidence from a bare assertion or accounting ambiguity.
Assess available evidence of payment capacity, default, concealed assets, or satisfaction of debts and expenses.
Account for any burden allocation or statutory presumption specific to the insolvency stage.
Use the debt and capacity findings as inputs to the separate procedural or discretionary decision.
example_application: A company contests a petition debt by relying on disputed intercompany accounts and alleged payments. Reconcile the records, test whether the dispute has a substantial evidential basis, and separately assess inability to pay.

template_name: Exceptional or Discretionary Remedy Evidence Check
description: Tests whether the applicant has established the evidential gateway for exceptional or discretionary relief and whether granting the relief would be necessary, useful, and proportionate.
application_scenario: Use for preventive injunctions, information-disclosure orders, insolvency orders, annulment, extensions, office-holder removal, or other remedies not granted automatically upon proving an underlying wrong.
reasoning_flow: Identify the remedy's purpose, threshold conditions, and factors guiding discretion.
Separate proof of the underlying right or wrong from proof that this particular remedy is justified.
Assess the strength, specificity, and immediacy of the evidence supporting the application.
Evaluate the practical utility of the order and whether it is likely to produce a worthwhile result.
Consider prejudice, delay, cost, alternative remedies, and the effect on third parties.
Check compliance with procedural safeguards, notice requirements, and candour obligations.
Reach the remedial determination on the established facts without using the remedy to fill evidential gaps.
example_application: An applicant seeks an order compelling an intermediary to disclose information after an alleged fraud. Assess the evidence of wrongdoing, the intermediary's connection, the likely value of disclosure, and whether a narrower alternative is available.

template_name: Third-Party Payment, Settlement, and Discharge Effect
description: Determines whether a payment, settlement, assignment, or arrangement involving a third party legally reduces or extinguishes the original debtor's obligation.
application_scenario: Use when payment is made by someone other than the debtor, settlement is reached with an intermediary or co-obligor, or a creditor's rights are said to have been transferred or satisfied.
reasoning_flow: Identify the original obligation, creditor, debtor, and the third party's role.
Establish the source, recipient, amount, and intended purpose of the payment or arrangement.
Determine whether the third party acted with authority and whether the creditor accepted performance in satisfaction of the obligation.
Examine the settlement terms for scope, reservation of rights, conditions, and treatment of co-obligors.
Distinguish payment, accord and satisfaction, assignment, novation, indemnity, and security.
Check whether any residual balance, recourse right, or subrogated claim remains.
Apply the proven legal effect to the original payment obligation.
example_application: A debtor argues that an arrangement with an intermediary resolved a dishonoured instrument. Determine whether the creditor authorized or accepted the arrangement as full satisfaction and whether any liability remained.

template_name: Adverse Possession Element Decomposition
description: Break an adverse-possession claim into the recurring requirements of factual possession, an intention to possess to the exclusion of others, continuity for the legally required period, and the absence of a legally effective basis making the occupation non-adverse.
application_scenario: Use when a possessor claims title or resists recovery of land by relying on long occupation.
reasoning_flow: Identify the precise land or portion of land said to have been possessed.
Determine whether the claimant exercised a sufficient degree of physical custody and control over that land.
Determine whether the claimant's conduct objectively communicated an intention to possess the land to the exclusion of the paper owner and strangers.
Construct the period of qualifying possession and test whether it was continuous for the applicable limitation period.
Check whether permission, licence, tenancy, acknowledgment of another's title, abandonment, or another interruption prevented the possession from being adverse.
Connect the element findings to the claimed possessory or limitation-based legal consequence.
example_application: A person occupying a defined parcel relies on enclosure, exclusive access, maintenance, and long uninterrupted use. The analysis separately tests physical control, exclusionary intent, duration, and whether the occupation began or continued with the owner's permission.

template_name: Objective Acts of Exclusive Control
description: Evaluate factual possession by combining outward acts of control over the land and distinguishing acts that indicate exclusive dominion from ordinary, shared, temporary, or equivocal use.
application_scenario: Use when the evidence consists of conduct such as occupying structures, enclosing land, controlling keys or access, storing goods, leasing space, paying outgoings, or making improvements.
reasoning_flow: List each physical act connected to the disputed land and identify its duration and frequency.
Classify each act as exclusionary control, ordinary use, maintenance, financial responsibility, or merely incidental presence.
Assess whether barriers, locks, gates, structures, access control, or dealings with third parties enabled the occupier to control who could enter or use the land.
Consider the nature and size of the land when deciding what acts of possession are reasonably possible.
Evaluate the acts cumulatively rather than treating any single act as automatically decisive.
Separate evidence of physical control from evidence that only suggests ownership beliefs or expenditure.
example_application: An occupier uses a small enclosed area, keeps the only key, maintains it, and permits others to enter on limited terms. Those acts are assessed together and in light of the area's physical character.

template_name: Permission or Licence Counterargument
description: Test whether occupation was permissive rather than adverse by examining how entry began, the parties' relationship, any rent or licence arrangement, later changes in terms, and whether permission was terminated or clearly repudiated.
application_scenario: Use when the paper owner alleges that residence or use occurred through consent, family accommodation, tenancy at will, licence, employment, or another consensual arrangement.
reasoning_flow: Identify the asserted source of permission and the person said to have granted it.
Examine the circumstances of initial entry, including any rent, licence fee, family arrangement, business relationship, or owner-authorized use.
Determine whether the permission covered the whole disputed area and the full period relied on.
Identify any event that terminated, withdrew, or clearly repudiated the permission.
Assess whether later acts objectively conveyed possession inconsistent with the continuing permission.
Start any adverse-possession period only when occupation became legally adverse rather than merely when physical occupation began.
example_application: A resident entered through a family arrangement and later changed locks and paid all property expenses. The analysis asks whether those later acts ended or contradicted the original permission and, if so, when the adverse period began.

template_name: Continuity and Tacking Across Occupiers
description: Determine whether periods of possession by different occupiers can form one continuous adverse-possession period by tracing succession, transfer of control, shared intention, and any gap or abandonment.
application_scenario: Use when possession is attributed to family members, predecessors in title, tenants, business successors, estates, or later purchasers rather than one occupier throughout.
reasoning_flow: Create a chronological sequence of every person said to have possessed the land.
For each transition, identify how physical control passed from one occupier to the next.
Determine whether the earlier occupier abandoned possession before the successor took control.
Check whether the successor continued possession of the same defined land under a sufficiently connected claim.
Exclude intervals in which the land returned to the paper owner's possession or ceased to be adversely possessed.
Aggregate only legally connectable periods before testing the limitation threshold.
example_application: Several related occupiers successively use the same enclosed premises. Their periods are combined only after confirming an uninterrupted handover of control and no intervening abandonment.

template_name: Limitation Accrual and Interruption Timeline
description: Build a legally relevant timeline to identify when the paper owner's right to recover land accrued, whether time was reset or suspended, and when the applicable limitation period expired.
application_scenario: Use when the dispute turns on the starting date of adverse possession, statutory changes, acknowledgments of title, demands, re-entry, renewed permission, or other possible interruptions.
reasoning_flow: Identify the earliest event said to constitute dispossession or discontinuance of the paper owner's possession.
Distinguish physical occupation from the later point, if any, at which that occupation became adverse.
Apply the limitation rule governing the relevant period and property interest.
Check for acknowledgments of title, payments, demands, recovery attempts, re-entry, abandonment, or statutory events that may affect the running of time.
Recalculate the qualifying period after each potentially interrupting event.
Determine the limitation consequence only after the complete timeline has been tested.
example_application: Occupation began under an uncertain arrangement, later became exclusive, and was followed by communications recognizing the registered owner. The timeline determines whether those communications altered the running of time.

template_name: Paper Owner Inactivity as Corroborative Evidence
description: Assess the evidential significance of the paper owner's failure to enter, demand rent, assert title, or seek recovery, while avoiding the inference that inactivity alone establishes adverse possession.
application_scenario: Use when the possessor relies on a long absence of objections, demands, inspections, rent collection, or repossession efforts.
reasoning_flow: Identify what acts the paper owner could reasonably have taken to assert possession or control.
Record whether the owner made demands, collected rent, entered the land, controlled access, granted permission, or commenced recovery action.
Compare the owner's inactivity with the occupier's positive acts of physical control and exclusionary intent.
Consider whether the parties' relationship or property arrangement explains the absence of owner intervention.
Treat inactivity as corroborative context rather than a substitute for proving possession and intention.
Use the combined evidence to evaluate whether the owner's right of recovery remained unexercised during the qualifying period.
example_application: The registered owner neither visits nor demands payment for a long period, while the occupier controls access and deals with the premises as an exclusive possessor. The absence of owner action reinforces, but does not independently establish, the claim.

template_name: Possessable Subject Matter and Boundary Identification
description: Confirm that the claimed subject matter is sufficiently identifiable and capable of the asserted possession, especially when it is a wall, common area, small strip, enclosed portion, structure, or land extending beyond registered boundaries.
application_scenario: Use when the dispute concerns only part of a property or when plans, physical features, and legal descriptions do not clearly align.
reasoning_flow: Define the claimed area using plans, title records, structures, enclosures, access points, and observable boundaries.
Distinguish the claimed area from adjoining land and from any larger premises occupied by the claimant.
Ask whether the physical character of the area permits acts amounting to possession.
Match each alleged possessory act to the specific area rather than to the property generally.
Resolve competing boundary descriptions or identify the evidential gap that prevents resolution.
Proceed to the possession analysis only for the area that is sufficiently identified.
example_application: A claimant occupies a narrow external portion adjoining a shop. The analysis first fixes the portion's boundaries and then asks whether the acts performed there amount to control of that particular area.

template_name: Declaratory Relief Despite Non-Participation
description: Require affirmative proof and an appropriate basis for declaratory relief even when the opposing party defaults, does not defend, or indicates no objection.
application_scenario: Use when a claimant seeks a declaration of possessory title, extinguishment, or unenforceability in undefended or default proceedings.
reasoning_flow: Confirm proper service and the procedural basis for deciding the application without a contested trial.
Identify the precise declaration requested and the legal elements necessary to justify it.
Examine whether admissible evidence establishes those elements despite the absence of opposing submissions.
Consider whether affected interests, uncertain boundaries, or missing parties make the declaration unsafe or incomplete.
Apply any discretionary limits governing declaratory relief.
Frame any declaration no more broadly than the rights and property proved.
example_application: A registered owner does not participate in a claim concerning long possession. The court still tests the land identity, possession evidence, limitation period, and proper scope of any declaration.

template_name: Ancient Mortgage or Security Limitation Analysis
description: Assess whether an old mortgage or registered security remains enforceable by tracing the secured interest, possession and succession, repayment or demand history, the applicable limitation rule, and the juridical form of the requested declaration.
application_scenario: Use when a current landholder seeks to clear an old mortgage or security entry after a prolonged period without repayment demands or enforcement.
reasoning_flow: Identify the security interest, the land it affects, and the chain of persons claiming under the mortgagor and mortgagee.
Determine whether principal, interest, rent, or another secured obligation was paid, acknowledged, or demanded during the relevant period.
Identify any possession, enforcement, discharge, or recognition inconsistent with the claimed lapse.
Apply the limitation rule governing enforcement of the security and recovery of secured property or money.
Distinguish between relief operating against a person and relief defining the status of the property or registered interest.
Check whether precedent-based objections concern jurisdiction, procedural nullity, or the substantive enforceability of the security.
example_application: A landholder encounters a very old registered charge with no recent demand or payment history. The analysis reconstructs the chain of title, searches for acknowledgment or enforcement, and tests the legal form of the requested declaration.

template_name: Contributory Negligence Allocation
description: After examining primary negligence, evaluate whether the injured person failed to take reasonable care for personal safety and, if so, allocate responsibility in light of causative potency, blameworthiness, workplace pressures, and emergency context.
application_scenario: Use in accident or occupiers' liability cases where the defendant alleges that the injured person contributed to the harm.
reasoning_flow: Identify the defendant's alleged breach and its causal contribution to the accident.
Identify the claimant's act or omission said to show a failure to take reasonable care.
Assess what risks were reasonably apparent to the claimant in the circumstances.
Consider whether instructions, defective equipment, time pressure, an emergency, or an attempt to protect persons or property affected the claimant's choice.
Compare the causative potency and blameworthiness of the respective conduct.
Translate any shared responsibility into an apportioned reduction before assessing recoverable damages.
example_application: A worker reacts quickly to a dangerous situation created by defective equipment and suffers injury. The analysis distinguishes an understandable emergency response from an unreasonable acceptance of an obvious risk before apportioning responsibility.

template_name: Select the Closest Material Analogy
description: Select and use an earlier authority by comparing the legal proposition, operative facts, and rationale rather than relying on broad subject-matter similarity.
application_scenario: Use when several authorities concern the same general field but differ in the legal mechanism, factual trigger, procedural setting, or policy rationale.
reasoning_flow: Define the precise legal proposition that requires authority.
Extract the governing rule and rationale from each candidate authority.
Identify the facts that were material to the earlier court's reasoning.
Compare those material facts and the legal mechanism with the present dispute.
Assess whether each difference changes the force of the earlier rationale.
Use the closest analogy at the appropriate level of abstraction and state any limits on its application.
example_application: When two earlier decisions address conditional entitlements, compare the condition, timing, beneficiary position, and purpose of the condition before using either decision to interpret the present entitlement.

template_name: Distinguish an Apparently Relevant Precedent
description: Determine whether an apparently relevant authority should have reduced influence because a factual, legal, or procedural difference undermines the rationale that made the earlier result appropriate.
application_scenario: Use when a party invokes a facially similar authority but the current dispute may involve a different statutory purpose, instrument wording, evidentiary setting, or discretionary standard.
reasoning_flow: State the proposition for which the authority is invoked.
Identify the authority's controlling rationale rather than only its result.
Locate the factual, textual, legal, or procedural feature that may distinguish the present dispute.
Explain whether that feature is material to the controlling rationale.
Retain any general principle that remains transferable despite the distinction.
Apply the transferable principle without treating the earlier factual resolution as automatic.
example_application: An authority involving exceptional complexity may be distinguished where the present matter turns mainly on settled principles and case-specific facts, while its general public-interest framework remains relevant.

template_name: Interpret an Instrument Through Text, Scheme, and Purpose
description: Resolve disputed wording in a statute, will, trust, deed, or procedural rule by integrating ordinary meaning, internal structure, purpose, and applicable interpretive principles.
application_scenario: Use when entitlement, authority, restriction, or administrative power depends on the meaning of written legal language.
reasoning_flow: Isolate the exact words that create the interpretive dispute.
Read those words in their immediate clause and in the instrument as a whole.
Identify the legal and practical purpose served by the provision.
Reconcile general language with specific language and avoid rendering any provision ineffective.
Apply relevant interpretive canons only where they clarify the text and structure.
Check analogous authorities involving comparable wording or legal mechanisms.
Adopt the construction that best fits the text, scheme, and lawful purpose together.
example_application: Where one clause appears to delay transfer while another gives a broader entitlement earlier, read both clauses together, identify the function of the delay, and compare authorities involving similarly structured gifts.

template_name: Adapt an Existing Right or Trust to Legal Change
description: Assess whether a later change in law, public institutions, or legal terminology alters a pre-existing right or purpose, or merely requires adaptation of its administrative machinery.
application_scenario: Use when an older instrument, family status, trust, or entitlement is evaluated after repeal, institutional replacement, constitutional change, or changed social conditions.
reasoning_flow: Identify the right, purpose, status, or obligation as it existed before the change.
Determine the legally relevant date and whether any interest had already accrued or vested.
Separate the substantive purpose from the office, label, or procedure originally used to carry it out.
Examine transitional provisions, preservation rules, and legislative purpose.
Assess whether literal discontinuity would frustrate the continuing substantive purpose.
Use analogous authorities to determine whether functional substitution or updated interpretation is permissible.
Apply the current legal framework while preserving valid pre-existing substance where the law allows.
example_application: If an instrument assigns a continuing function to an office that no longer exists, determine whether the office was essential to the purpose or only the mechanism for administering it.

template_name: Establish Legal Status Through Converging Evidence
description: Determine identity, kinship, dependency, or beneficiary status by testing multiple forms of evidence against the governing legal definition.
application_scenario: Use when inheritance, estate administration, compensation, or another entitlement depends on proving who a person is or how that person is legally related to another.
reasoning_flow: Define the exact legal status that must be established and the applicable legal criteria.
Collect documentary, testimonial, conduct-based, and customary evidence relevant to that status.
Reconcile inconsistent names, records, household roles, or historical practices.
Distinguish social treatment or factual dependency from the legal requirements for the claimed status.
Evaluate the evidence cumulatively and address material gaps or alternative explanations.
Carry the status determination forward to the entitlement or procedural consequence that depends on it.
example_application: Where records use different names and the claimed entitlement depends on family relationship, compare official documents, long-term conduct, family evidence, and the governing definition before determining the person's legal capacity.

template_name: Exercise Procedural or Protective Discretion by Structured Balancing
description: Apply a discretionary standard by identifying its threshold, weighing relevant factors, and selecting an arrangement that advances the governing protective or procedural objective with proportionate disruption.
application_scenario: Use for applications involving representation, joinder, appointment, child welfare, management of property, or another remedy governed by justice, welfare, suitability, necessity, or public interest.
reasoning_flow: Identify the source and purpose of the court's discretion.
Determine any threshold requirements that must be met before balancing begins.
List the legally relevant factors and exclude considerations outside the statutory or procedural purpose.
Assess necessity, suitability, practical benefit, prejudice, delay, cost, and available alternatives.
Give priority to any expressly paramount interest, such as a child's welfare or protection of affected persons.
Compare the proposed arrangement with less disruptive workable alternatives.
Record how the factors interact rather than treating any single factor as automatically decisive.
example_application: When choosing between competing arrangements for a protected person's future, compare concrete educational, developmental, logistical, and continuity factors under the paramount-interest standard.

template_name: Evaluate a Conduct-Based Legal Threshold Cumulatively
description: Determine whether a course of conduct crosses a legal threshold by assessing proved acts in context, their cumulative effect, and the governing objective standard.
application_scenario: Use when liability or relief depends on unreasonable behavior, non-cooperation, fraud-related conduct, acquiescence, breach, or another evaluative characterization of conduct.
reasoning_flow: State the conduct-based legal threshold and whose perspective the standard adopts.
Separate proved acts from allegations, inferences, and background friction.
Evaluate credibility, contemporaneous records, admissions, and consistency of explanations.
Consider each act in context, including vulnerability, duration, repetition, and practical consequences.
Assess the cumulative pattern rather than requiring every incident to satisfy the threshold independently.
Address innocent explanations, reconciliation, waiver, delay, or later conduct that may alter the inference.
Apply the objective standard to the established pattern and identify the facts doing the most legal work.
example_application: A series of acts, omissions, disputed explanations, and later attempts to remedy the situation should be evaluated as a whole rather than as unrelated incidents.

template_name: Quantify Multiple Heads of Financial Relief Without Overlap
description: Calculate several monetary heads using a common factual foundation while keeping distinct losses separate and preventing duplication, inconsistent assumptions, or recovery twice for the same economic interest.
application_scenario: Use in fatal-accident, personal-injury, estate, or family financial proceedings involving several pecuniary and conventional components.
reasoning_flow: List each legally available head of relief and its distinct compensatory purpose.
Identify the evidence required for income, dependency, savings, expenses, duration, and contingencies.
Choose a consistent valuation method and time horizon for each pecuniary head.
Apply conventional or statutory components separately from evidence-based pecuniary calculations.
Check whether any payment, compensation, asset, or benefit corresponds to the same loss and reaches the same recipient group.
Remove overlaps or apply any legally required set-off without reducing unrelated heads.
Calculate interest from the legally appropriate point and verify the aggregate for internal consistency.
example_application: A dependency calculation and an estate-based accumulation calculation may draw on the same earnings evidence, but their purposes and expense assumptions must remain distinct before any aggregate figure is formed.

template_name: Analyze Causation, Scope of Responsibility, and Mitigation in Sequence
description: Evaluate responsibility for harm through a staged inquiry that separates factual causation, legal attribution, intervening events, and avoidable post-harm loss.
application_scenario: Use when an alleged wrong is followed by physical, psychiatric, financial, or dependency loss and the parties dispute whether later events or claimant conduct changed the extent of responsibility.
reasoning_flow: Define the specific wrong and each distinct item of alleged harm.
Test factual causation using the appropriate counterfactual and available evidence.
Assess whether the harm falls within the risk, duty, or legal responsibility created by the wrong.
Examine foreseeability, natural consequence, remoteness, and any independent intervening event.
Separate initial injury from later aggravation or continuation of loss.
Evaluate reasonable mitigation steps and determine the portion of avoidable loss, if any.
Apply the causation findings separately to each head of loss before composing the overall assessment.
example_application: Where later statements are alleged to worsen an existing psychiatric condition, distinguish the original injury, the claimed aggravation, other contributing causes, and the effect of delayed treatment.

template_name: Compose a Multi-Issue Decision Through Dependency-Aware Sequencing
description: Resolve a complex claim by decomposing it into legally distinct issues, sequencing dependent questions, and recombining the findings without contradiction or double counting.
application_scenario: Use when a single requested remedy depends on several threshold, status, interpretation, conduct, causation, or quantum questions.
reasoning_flow: Translate the requested remedy into the legal questions that must be answered.
Separate threshold issues from merits, defenses, remedy, and quantum.
Map dependencies so that status, jurisdiction, interpretation, or entitlement questions are addressed before downstream calculations.
Assign the governing rule, burden, material facts, and missing information to each issue.
Resolve each issue only to the level needed for the next dependent step.
Check findings across issues for factual and legal consistency.
Combine the issue-level determinations into a remedy analysis that reflects all prerequisites and avoids counting the same fact or loss twice.
example_application: An estate claim may require identity, relationship, governing-instrument construction, and entitlement questions to be resolved in that order before any administrative direction is formulated.

template_name: Issue-Directed Long-Fact Filtering
description: Condense a lengthy factual record into an issue-specific set of operative facts, separating legally material events from background, repetition, and collateral detail.
application_scenario: Use when a contract or related civil dispute contains a long chronology but only a limited subset of events bears on formation, performance, breach, liability, or remedy.
reasoning_flow: Convert each disputed issue into a small set of factual propositions that must be established.
Assign each fact to one or more propositions and mark its temporal position in the transaction.
Prioritize contemporaneous documents, payments, deliveries, notices, admissions, and conduct over remote background.
Separate operative facts from credibility facts, contextual facts, and duplicative narrative.
Build a compact issue-specific timeline and record material conflicts or missing links without resolving unrelated matters.
example_application: In a supply dispute with extensive correspondence, retain the order, agreed delivery conditions, actual deliveries, objections, payment instrument, and later cancellation communications while omitting unrelated corporate history.

template_name: Contracting Party and Obligation Holder Identification
description: Identify which person or entity entered the relevant legal relationship and which actor actually held or assumed the disputed obligation.
application_scenario: Use when several companies, agents, intermediaries, subtenants, affiliates, directors, or service providers appear in the transaction and liability depends on selecting the correct obligor or beneficiary.
reasoning_flow: List every agreement, instrument, or arrangement and the parties expressly named in each.
Distinguish principals from agents, intermediaries, affiliates, assignees, subcontractors, and persons acting only in a representative capacity.
Trace which actor requested, received, performed, invoiced, paid for, or controlled the relevant subject matter.
Examine later conduct for an assumption, substitution, assignment, acknowledgment, or continuation of the obligation.
Determine the party relationship relevant to the disputed duty before assessing breach or monetary liability.
example_application: Where work was arranged through related companies, compare the written engagement, invoices, payment history, managerial directions, and any oral substitution to identify which company bore the payment obligation.

template_name: Contract Terms Reconstruction from Fragmented Evidence
description: Reconstruct the operative agreement when its terms are dispersed across formal documents, informal writings, oral discussions, and subsequent conduct.
application_scenario: Use when the parties agree that a transaction existed but dispute its scope, price, timing, subject matter, compensation structure, or other essential terms.
reasoning_flow: Collect every alleged source of terms, including signed documents, letters, faxes, notes, invoices, oral statements, and collateral arrangements.
Separate express terms from terms inferred from conduct or commercial context.
Compare the sources for consistency on the identity of the parties, subject matter, price, timing, conditions, and allocation of responsibility.
Use subsequent performance, payment, access, delivery, and objection patterns to test competing accounts of the agreement.
Produce a consolidated term matrix that records the most reliable formulation of each disputed obligation and any unresolved ambiguity.
example_application: For an unwritten employment arrangement, combine the hiring discussion, informal written notes, actual salary payments, bonus discussions, later variation meeting, and employer correspondence to reconstruct the compensation and termination terms.

template_name: Disputed Transfer Characterization
description: Determine the legal character of a money or asset transfer by examining its purpose, documentation, destination, benefit, accounting treatment, and surrounding relationship rather than relying on a single label.
application_scenario: Use when one side describes a transfer as a loan, temporary advance, purchase payment, settlement, deposit, reimbursement, or internal adjustment and the other side gives it a different character.
reasoning_flow: Identify the source, recipient, destination, and ultimate beneficiary of the transfer.
Record the descriptions used in contemporaneous vouchers, bank records, agreements, correspondence, and accounts.
Compare the stated purpose with how the funds or assets were actually used.
Examine repayment behavior, settlement language, bookkeeping entries, and whether the transfer satisfied another obligation.
Classify the transfer according to the transaction that best explains the full documentary and conduct record.
example_application: A payment described informally as temporary funding is traced through banking records to an acquisition benefiting a related party, then compared with later account entries and alleged repayment conduct to determine its true legal character.

template_name: Obligation-to-Performance Mapping and Breach Attribution
description: Match each contractual obligation to the actor responsible for it, compare the promised and actual performance, and attribute non-performance while accounting for dependencies between the parties' duties.
application_scenario: Use in disputes involving incomplete work, delayed delivery, non-payment, refusal to accept performance, defective performance, or competing allegations that the other side breached first.
reasoning_flow: Break the agreement into discrete duties, conditions, deadlines, quantities, and performance standards.
Assign each duty to the responsible party and identify any duty that depended on prior cooperation or performance by the other side.
Place actual deliveries, work, payments, instructions, refusals, and interruptions against the corresponding duties.
Distinguish complete, partial, late, defective, prevented, excused, and unperformed obligations.
Identify the earliest material departure and evaluate whether it caused or justified later non-performance.
example_application: In a subcontract dispute, map responsibility for transport, labor, equipment, and site access, then compare the agreed allocation with breakdowns, work stoppage, replacement contracting, and completion by another contractor.

template_name: Later Variation, Waiver, and Course-of-Dealing Assessment
description: Assess whether later communications or conduct changed, relaxed, replaced, or merely discussed an original contractual requirement.
application_scenario: Use when the parties depart from written schedules, alter the responsible party, continue a relationship after a triggering event, or rely on informal communications as modifying strict terms.
reasoning_flow: State the original term alleged to have been changed or waived.
Identify the later words or conduct said to alter that term and verify the authority of the actors involved.
Test whether the later material shows mutual assent, a unilateral indulgence, temporary accommodation, or mere negotiation.
Examine reliance, repeated practice, acceptance of changed performance, and any reservation of strict rights.
Define the scope and duration of any effective variation or waiver and determine whether the original term was later reinstated.
example_application: Where shipment schedules were repeatedly adjusted through messages and accepted performance, analyze whether the exchanges created a binding revised timetable or only ad hoc accommodations.

template_name: Delivery, Acceptance, and Payment Maturity
description: Determine whether the required performance was delivered or made available, whether it was accepted or rejected, and whether the corresponding payment obligation became due.
application_scenario: Use in claims for the price of goods, services, work, or transferred property where delivery, acceptance, access, completeness, or failure of consideration is disputed.
reasoning_flow: Define the contractual standard for delivery or completion, including place, time, quantity, condition, and any documentary requirement.
Identify direct evidence of handover, access, possession, use, inspection, acknowledgment, or tender of performance.
Compare contemporaneous objections with later denials and determine whether any rejection was timely and specific.
Assess whether acceptance, retention, use, or a payment instrument indicates recognition of performance.
Determine whether payment matured fully, partially, or not at all, accounting for any proven deficiency in performance.
example_application: For goods allegedly sold and delivered, compare access to the premises, witness observations, inventory gaps, later possession, and the absence or timing of objections before deciding whether the price became payable.

template_name: Termination Event and Continuing Rights Analysis
description: Identify the legally operative termination event, determine whether required notice or authority existed, and separate rights that ended from obligations that had already accrued.
application_scenario: Use when a relationship allegedly ended through dismissal, resignation, cancellation, re-entry, abandonment, expiry, or refusal to continue performance.
reasoning_flow: Identify every alleged termination event and place them in chronological order.
Determine who had authority to terminate and what notice, condition, or contractual trigger applied.
Compare the parties' words with their immediate conduct, including continued occupation, work, payment, access, or replacement performance.
Determine the effective termination point and the legal status of conduct occurring afterward.
Separate prospective obligations from accrued payment, restitution, possession, accounting, or damage claims.
example_application: When one side says an employee resigned and the other says the employment was ended without notice, examine the meeting, departure, confirmatory communication, proposed payment, and subsequent conduct to identify the operative event and accrued compensation.

template_name: Monetary Remedy, Deduction, and Set-Off Accounting
description: Convert established liability into a net monetary position by testing the legal basis, causation, proof, reasonableness, and overlap of each claimed amount or deduction.
application_scenario: Use when a party seeks unpaid compensation, contract price, replacement cost, deposit return, reinstatement expense, commission, or other monetary relief subject to deductions or countervailing losses.
reasoning_flow: List each claimed component and tie it to a contractual or legal entitlement.
Separate accrued debt from compensatory loss, restitution, accounting relief, and contingent or estimated amounts.
For each loss or deduction, verify causation, actual incurrence, evidential proof, reasonableness, and mitigation.
Exclude hypothetical work, unrelated expenditure, duplicated recovery, and amounts already satisfied or credited.
Calculate the net position after valid payments, deductions, set-offs, and replacement-performance consequences.
example_application: A deposit-return claim is analyzed by separating work actually performed from estimated reinstatement, checking whether each item was caused by a contractual breach, and crediting only proven and non-duplicative expenditure.

template_name: Competing Narrative and Evidence Reliability Resolution
description: Resolve conflicting accounts by testing each narrative against contemporaneous documents, objective conduct, financial records, internal consistency, corroboration, and commercial probability.
application_scenario: Use when liability depends on disputed conversations, suspicious documents, inconsistent testimony, unexplained accounting entries, or later recollections that conflict with objective records.
reasoning_flow: State the competing factual narratives in neutral and comparable terms.
Identify objective anchors such as signed records, bank movements, delivery evidence, CCTV, invoices, notices, and undisputed conduct.
Test each account for internal consistency, consistency over time, corroboration, and compatibility with the objective anchors.
Examine document provenance, timing, alterations, silence in response to communications, and incentives to reconstruct events.
Adopt only the factual findings necessary to resolve the legal issue and mark any residual uncertainty.
example_application: When witnesses disagree about whether goods remained at a property, compare their opportunities to observe, access records, contemporaneous documents, physical features, later possession, and the commercial plausibility of each account.

template_name: Negligence Case Issue Sequencing
description: Structures a multi-issue negligence dispute so that factual reconstruction, breach, shared fault, derivative liability, causation, and damages are addressed in a legally coherent order.
application_scenario: Use when a personal-injury or accident claim contains several interdependent questions rather than a single liability issue.
reasoning_flow: Identify the alleged accident, injury, responsible actors, and requested categories of compensation.
Separate the dispute into accident reconstruction, primary negligence, claimant or third-party fault, derivative liability, causation, and damages issues as applicable.
Mark which issues must be resolved before later issues can be assessed.
Assign the material facts and governing rules to the issue they directly bear on.
Resolve the issues in dependency order and carry only established findings into later stages.
Combine the issue-level determinations into one internally consistent liability-and-damages analysis.
example_application: A roadway injury dispute involves conflicting accounts of the collision, allegations against two drivers, a claim of pedestrian fault, and several heads of future loss. The template orders the analysis from what happened, to each actor's negligence, to allocation of responsibility, and finally to recoverable loss.

template_name: Accident Reconstruction from Competing Evidence
description: Reconstructs how an accident occurred by comparing competing narratives with objective conditions, contemporaneous records, corroboration, and physical evidence.
application_scenario: Use when the location, sequence, mechanism, or participants' movements are disputed.
reasoning_flow: List each materially different account of the accident without merging them.
Extract the points of agreement and the precise factual conflicts among the accounts.
Map objective evidence such as damage patterns, photographs, road layout, lighting, weather, medical findings, or scene conditions to each disputed point.
Check each account for internal consistency, consistency with earlier statements, and independent corroboration.
Prefer the reconstruction that best explains the full body of reliable evidence with the fewest unresolved contradictions.
State the reconstructed sequence at the level needed for the later negligence and causation issues.
example_application: A pedestrian and a driver disagree about whether contact occurred with the person or an object being carried. Earlier statements, the injury pattern, vehicle position, and scene geometry are compared to identify the most plausible mechanism.

template_name: Reasonable-Care Breach Assessment
description: Evaluates whether an actor failed to take reasonable care by connecting foreseeable risk, surrounding circumstances, available precautions, and the conduct actually taken.
application_scenario: Use for alleged negligent driving, unsafe premises, unsafe work systems, or other conduct creating a risk of personal injury.
reasoning_flow: Identify the actor, activity, and foreseeable class of persons exposed to harm.
Specify the risk that a reasonable person in the actor's position should have recognized.
Determine the precautions reasonably available in light of visibility, speed, traffic, workplace conditions, premises defects, equipment, instructions, and other contextual factors.
Compare the actor's actual conduct with those precautions and any applicable operational rule.
Distinguish a mere accident from a failure to keep proper lookout, control the activity, warn, maintain, instruct, equip, or otherwise reduce the identified risk.
Record the breach finding in terms that can be used in the causation and responsibility-allocation stages.
example_application: An operator proceeds through a constrained area despite limited visibility and nearby vulnerable persons. The analysis asks what lookout, speed, warning, positioning, or stopping precautions were reasonably required and compares them with the conduct shown by the evidence.

template_name: Multi-Actor Fault and Apportionment
description: Assesses the conduct of several actors separately and allocates responsibility when more than one person's lack of care contributed to the same accident.
application_scenario: Use when a claimant, defendant, third party, or multiple drivers are each alleged to have contributed to the harm.
reasoning_flow: Define the relevant conduct and standard of care for each actor independently.
Determine whether each actor departed from the applicable standard.
Link each proven departure to the occurrence or severity of the accident rather than treating fault as purely moral blame.
Compare the causal potency and relative blameworthiness of the contributing acts.
Translate that comparison into an allocation of responsibility under the applicable apportionment framework.
Apply the allocation consistently to the damages stage without double counting the same conduct.
example_application: Two vehicles enter a junction on intersecting paths, while one passenger also alleges unsafe conduct by a third road user. Each actor's lookout, speed, signaling, and positioning are assessed separately before responsibility is allocated.

template_name: Injury Causation and Attribution
description: Determines which injuries and limitations are attributable to the accident and separates them from unrelated, pre-existing, later-arising, or insufficiently proven conditions.
application_scenario: Use when the claimant presents multiple symptoms, delayed complaints, degenerative conditions, disputed diagnoses, or mixed medical causes.
reasoning_flow: Create a timeline of the accident, immediate symptoms, treatment, later complaints, and functional changes.
Match each claimed injury or limitation to contemporaneous records and medical opinion.
Identify pre-existing, degenerative, intervening, or unrelated conditions that may explain part of the presentation.
Assess whether the accident caused, aggravated, accelerated, or merely coincided with each condition.
Define the duration and extent of accident-related impairment for each accepted condition.
Pass only the accident-attributable consequences to the damages calculation.
example_application: A claimant has an acute fracture, later-reported symptoms, and an asymptomatic degenerative condition that becomes painful after the incident. The template distinguishes direct injury, possible aggravation, and complaints lacking a sufficient causal link.

template_name: Credibility and Inconsistency Evaluation
description: Evaluates disputed testimony through a structured comparison of internal consistency, prior accounts, objective evidence, motive, and independent corroboration.
application_scenario: Use when liability or damages depend on inconsistent versions of events or changing descriptions of injury and need.
reasoning_flow: Identify every material proposition that depends on testimonial credibility.
Compare each witness's account across pleadings, statements, reports, and oral evidence.
Separate minor memory variation from contradictions affecting the central mechanism, conduct, injury, or claimed need.
Test the account against objective evidence and independent witnesses.
Consider whether any inconsistency has a plausible explanation and whether it affects only one issue or the witness's broader reliability.
Make issue-specific credibility findings rather than accepting or discarding an entire account wholesale.
example_application: A claimant changes the description of how contact occurred, while another witness provides partial corroboration and the medical evidence fits only one version. The analysis evaluates the contradiction only to the extent it bears on the accident mechanism and resulting injury.

template_name: Derivative and Institutional Liability
description: Determines whether a person or organization bears legal responsibility for harm caused by another actor or by conditions within property, equipment, or work systems under its control.
application_scenario: Use when the immediate actor is not the only potential defendant, such as an employer, vehicle owner, premises owner, manager, or operating organization.
reasoning_flow: Identify the immediate negligent act or unsafe condition and the person who directly created or controlled it.
Identify each additional defendant's relationship to the actor, property, vehicle, activity, or work system.
Select the applicable basis of derivative or institutional responsibility, such as employment scope, authorization, control, maintenance duty, or provision of a safe system.
Test the required relationship and connection between the underlying wrong and the additional defendant.
Keep direct negligence and derivative responsibility analytically separate.
Carry any established responsibility into the allocation and damages stages without duplicating the same liability basis.
example_application: An accident involves a vehicle driver and the organization connected with the vehicle, or an unsafe workplace task arranged by an employer. The template first assesses the immediate conduct and then asks whether the relevant relationship or control basis extends responsibility to the organization.

template_name: Personal-Injury Damages by Head of Loss
description: Organizes personal-injury compensation into distinct heads of past and future loss, each tied to causation, evidence, duration, and avoidance of overlap.
application_scenario: Use after liability and injury attribution have been addressed in a non-fatal personal-injury claim.
reasoning_flow: List each claimed head of non-pecuniary, financial, medical, care, equipment, accommodation, transport, and miscellaneous loss.
Separate past loss already incurred from future loss requiring projection.
For each head, identify the accident-related need, evidential foundation, calculation method, and relevant period.
Test whether the expense or loss is reasonable, necessary, and causally connected to the injury.
Check for overlap among earnings, domestic assistance, medical care, equipment, mobility, and general-damages components.
Aggregate only distinct, adequately evidenced heads and apply any responsibility adjustment at the proper stage.
example_application: A seriously injured claimant seeks compensation for pain, reduced earnings, ongoing treatment, domestic help, mobility equipment, and transport. Each category is assessed separately before the figures are combined.

template_name: Future Loss and Continuing-Need Projection
description: Projects future financial loss and care needs from present evidence while accounting for duration, life or working expectations, contingencies, and the evidential reliability of assumptions.
application_scenario: Use for future earnings, retirement benefits, medical treatment, domestic assistance, prostheses, equipment, or other continuing needs.
reasoning_flow: Identify the future loss stream or recurring need and its causal connection to the injury or death.
Establish the baseline rate using earnings records, employment history, medical recommendations, market cost, or other reliable evidence.
Define the probable duration using age, work expectancy, treatment prognosis, replacement cycles, or dependency period.
Adjust for promotion prospects, residual earning capacity, mortality, employment uncertainty, inflation or discounting rules, and other applicable contingencies.
Choose and explain the appropriate projection method, including multiplicand-and-multiplier reasoning where applicable.
Check the projected amount against related heads to prevent duplication or inconsistent assumptions.
example_application: A claimant has reduced work capacity and requires periodic treatment and assistance. The analysis establishes a baseline cost or income stream, estimates duration, applies appropriate contingencies, and keeps separate projections mutually consistent.

template_name: Fatal-Accident Dependency and Estate Loss
description: Separates and calculates losses arising from death by distinguishing dependants' lost contributions from losses belonging to the deceased's estate and from proven special expenses.
application_scenario: Use when death caused by a tort gives rise to claims by dependants, personal representatives, or the estate.
reasoning_flow: Identify the eligible claimants and separate dependency-based claims from estate-based claims.
Reconstruct the deceased's probable income, benefits, services, savings pattern, and personal expenditure.
Determine the portion of income or services that would probably have benefited each dependant.
Estimate the relevant dependency or working period and apply the governing projection method.
Assess estate losses and special expenses independently from dependency loss.
Check that the same income, service, or expense is not counted in more than one statutory or common-law category.
example_application: A deceased worker regularly contributed earnings and services to family members and also had employment benefits and funeral-related expenses. The template calculates family dependency, estate loss, and special expenses as separate components.

template_name: Proof of Claimed Loss and Expert Need
description: Tests whether a claimed injury-related expense, need, or financial loss is established by admissible and sufficiently reliable evidence.
application_scenario: Use when damages depend on expert reports, investigation records, receipts, employment records, or contested descriptions of future need.
reasoning_flow: Identify the factual proposition and damages head for which the evidence is offered.
Classify the evidence as direct testimony, contemporaneous document, expert opinion, investigation material, or later estimate.
Check admissibility, source knowledge, methodological basis, and whether the evidence depends on a disputed account.
Determine whether expert testimony is necessary to connect the injury to the claimed treatment, equipment, care, or functional need.
Compare the claim with receipts, wage records, treatment history, market evidence, and consistent prior descriptions.
Quantify only the portion that can be established with reasonable evidential certainty, using a justified estimate where exact proof is unavailable.
example_application: A claimant seeks specialized equipment, ongoing therapy, travel costs, and domestic assistance. The template examines whether each item is grounded in competent expert evidence, reliable cost material, and a consistent account of functional need.

template_name: Identify the Contracting Parties and Legal Capacity
description: Determines which persons or entities are bound by an agreement and whether an apparent intermediary acted as principal, agent, partner, lender, investor, or service provider.
application_scenario: Use when the existence of a transaction is accepted but the parties dispute who contracted with whom or how their relationship should be legally characterized.
reasoning_flow: List each plausible contracting party and the legal capacity attributed to that party.
Examine communications, forms, invoices, payment arrangements, delivery conduct, and prior dealings for objective indications of assent and capacity.
Distinguish conduct performed on a party's own account from conduct performed for a disclosed or undisclosed principal.
Characterize the transaction according to its substance rather than the label later assigned by either side.
Identify which obligations, payment rights, and liabilities follow from the resulting party structure.
example_application: A customer deals through an intermediary who uses another company's form. Determine whether the intermediary contracted personally or merely arranged performance for another entity before assessing payment liability.

template_name: Reconstruct Express and Implied Contractual Obligations
description: Reconstructs the operative obligations of the parties from written terms, oral communications, commercial context, and necessary implications.
application_scenario: Use when liability depends on the content of an incomplete, informal, oral, or disputed agreement, including timing, payment, cooperation, information, delivery, or completion obligations.
reasoning_flow: Collect the documents, communications, and conduct that record or evidence the agreement.
Separate express promises from background expectations and post-contract assertions.
Determine whether any additional term must be implied to make the arrangement workable or reflect an established course of dealing.
Specify each obligation, the party responsible, the required performance, and any deadline or condition.
Use the reconstructed obligation set as the baseline for later breach, payment, termination, and remedy analysis.
example_application: A business-transfer agreement requires cooperation but does not fully describe the information to be supplied. Identify the express duties and any necessary implied duty to provide materials essential to completion.

template_name: Determine Whether Performance Amounted to Contractual Breach
description: Tests alleged conduct against the operative contractual obligations to determine whether there was nonperformance, defective performance, delay, abandonment, or repudiatory conduct.
application_scenario: Use when one party alleges failure to deliver goods, complete services, provide required information, make payment, cooperate, or otherwise perform an agreed obligation.
reasoning_flow: Identify the precise obligation said to have been broken.
Determine when and how performance became due, including any relevant sequence or dependency between obligations.
Compare the required performance with the acts actually completed, omitted, delayed, or refused.
Assess whether any contractual excuse, condition, prevention by the other party, or accepted variation alters the performance standard.
Classify the failure by type and materiality so that downstream termination and remedy questions can be evaluated.
example_application: A supplier accepts a payment instrument but does not complete delivery. Compare the agreed payment-and-delivery sequence with the parties' conduct and classify any failure before assessing remedies.

template_name: Assess a Right to Suspend or Withhold Payment
description: Determines whether a party may delay or withhold money that would otherwise be payable because of an express condition, a genuine contingent liability, incomplete performance, or another recognized basis.
application_scenario: Use when a payer admits receiving value or funds but argues that payment is not yet due or may be retained pending another event.
reasoning_flow: Establish the amount or performance that would ordinarily trigger payment.
Identify the clause or doctrine relied on to postpone, suspend, retain, or set off payment.
Interpret whether the asserted event is a true condition precedent, a timing mechanism, a security measure, or merely a commercial concern.
Check whether the triggering contingency has actually occurred or is supported by concrete evidence rather than speculation.
Determine the portion, if any, that remains presently payable after applying the valid condition or adjustment.
example_application: A contractor receives money attributable to a subcontractor's completed work but retains it because a third party might later seek repayment. Determine whether the contract makes that possibility a valid condition for withholding.

template_name: Evaluate Contract Termination or Rescission Following Breach
description: Determines whether an alleged breach entitled the innocent party to terminate or rescind and whether the termination procedure and timing were legally effective.
application_scenario: Use when parties dispute who ended the agreement, whether a prior breach justified that step, or whether notice and election requirements were satisfied.
reasoning_flow: Identify the breach relied on as the basis for ending the agreement.
Assess whether the term breached or the consequences of the breach were sufficiently serious to justify termination or rescission.
Determine when the terminating party learned of the relevant facts and whether it clearly elected to end the contract.
Check compliance with contractual notice, cure, deadline, and communication requirements.
Separate obligations and remedies that accrued before termination from those affected by the termination itself.
example_application: A purchaser ends a transaction after repeated failures to provide completion materials. Determine whether those failures were sufficiently serious and whether the purchaser gave an effective notice of termination.

template_name: Test Affirmation, Waiver, or Loss of a Contractual Objection
description: Assesses whether a party that knew of a defect, misrepresentation, or breach nevertheless continued the contract in a manner that limits a later attempt to avoid liability.
application_scenario: Use when a party relies on an earlier defect but subsequently performed, accepted benefits, made payments, or otherwise treated the agreement as continuing.
reasoning_flow: Identify the defect, breach, or representation on which the later objection is based.
Determine when the objecting party obtained sufficient knowledge of the relevant facts.
Review subsequent conduct for continued performance, acceptance of benefits, payment, delay, or express confirmation.
Distinguish a temporary reservation of rights from an unequivocal election to continue the agreement.
Determine which objections or remedies remain available after accounting for affirmation, waiver, or reliance by the other party.
example_application: A contracting party learns of an alleged misrepresentation but continues working under the agreement. Evaluate whether that conduct preserved or relinquished the later attempt to avoid the contract.

template_name: Calculate the Outstanding Contractual Debt
description: Calculates the net amount presently due by reconciling the agreed price, additional authorized work, invoices, payments, credits, and legally available deductions.
application_scenario: Use when liability for some payment is established or largely uncontested but the amount due remains disputed.
reasoning_flow: Identify the contractual price or other primary monetary obligation.
Add charges for variations, additional work, goods, interest, or expenses only where authorization and contractual entitlement are established.
Match invoices and payment demands to the underlying work or goods.
Deduct proven payments, refunds, credits, agreed allowances, and valid set-offs without double counting.
Present the net balance and separately flag any component that depends on unresolved entitlement or evidence.
example_application: A service provider completed the original scope and additional approved work, while the customer made several partial payments. Reconcile the contractual charges and credits to determine the remaining balance.

template_name: Determine Whether a Later Transaction Discharged an Earlier Obligation
description: Determines whether a later payment, asset transfer, compromise, forfeiture, or settlement extinguished or modified an earlier debt or contractual claim.
application_scenario: Use when the parties agree that a later transaction occurred but dispute whether it was partial performance, collateral security, a separate transaction, or a full settlement.
reasoning_flow: Define the earlier obligation and the amount or performance then outstanding.
Identify the later transaction and the consideration exchanged.
Examine contemporaneous words and conduct for an objective intention to settle, substitute, secure, or partially satisfy the earlier obligation.
Check whether the alleged discharge satisfies any legal requirements for compromise, variation, or acceptance of substituted performance.
Allocate the later transaction as full discharge, partial credit, security, or a separate dealing for subsequent remedy analysis.
example_application: A debtor transfers an interest in property after receiving a loan. Determine whether the transfer was accepted as complete settlement, as partial repayment, or merely as security.

template_name: Measure Expectation and Loss-of-Bargain Damages
description: Measures the monetary position the claimant would have occupied if the contract had been properly performed, while excluding unsupported or guaranteed returns that were never promised.
application_scenario: Use after breach is established and the claimed loss concerns a missed purchase, resale margin, expected profit, or other contractual bargain.
reasoning_flow: Define the promised performance and the economic position expected on proper completion.
Select the legally relevant valuation point and a reliable measure such as market value, replacement cost, contract price differential, or provable net profit.
Deduct sums recovered, retained, refunded, or avoided because performance did not occur.
Distinguish a contractually protected expectation from a speculative projection or non-guaranteed profit.
State the recoverable loss components separately from interest, costs, and other ancillary relief.
example_application: A buyer loses a completed purchase after paying the price. Compare the contract price with reliable market evidence at the relevant time, then deduct money recovered or expenses avoided.

template_name: Analyze Causation, Mitigation, and Consequential Loss
