example_application: A company has mounting liabilities, incomplete accounts, and repeated failures to satisfy regulatory requirements. The template tests insolvency and noncompliance separately before considering restructuring, liquidation, or a narrower order.

template_name: Property Entitlement Before Allocation or Possession Remedy
description: Establish the parties' legal or beneficial interests in property before deciding possession, sale, partition, boundary, or distribution relief.
application_scenario: Use when ownership shares, title documents, long possession, boundaries, or competing proprietary claims must be resolved before a property remedy.
reasoning_flow: Identify each asserted source of legal, beneficial, or possessory entitlement.
Examine conveyances, registrations, succession documents, acknowledgments, plans, and possession history.
Resolve challenges to validity, boundaries, limitation, estoppel, or competing title.
Determine the parties' respective interests or shares.
Only then assess whether sale, partition, possession, declaration, or distribution is appropriate and how proceeds or rights should be allocated.
example_application: Co-owners disagree about their shares and whether the property should be sold. The template first resolves the source and size of each interest, then evaluates the available property remedy and distribution method.

template_name: Issue-Specific Fact Filtration
description: Convert a broad factual record into a compact issue-specific record by linking only legally material facts to the governing elements and the assigned burden.
application_scenario: Use when a case contains a lengthy chronology or many background facts but each issue turns on a narrower set of facts.
reasoning_flow: State the precise legal issue without embedding the requested disposition.
Identify the governing rule, test, or doctrinal elements and note which party bears each burden.
Sort the record into facts material to each element, facts relevant only to another issue, and background facts.
Separate facts tending in different directions and identify material evidentiary gaps.
Apply the filtered facts element by element and record an issue-level determination for later composition.
example_application: In a dispute with an extensive history of dealings, isolate the communications and conduct bearing on the disputed obligation, map them to formation and performance elements, and leave unrelated background events outside that issue analysis.

template_name: Merits-to-Remedy Dependency Chain
description: Sequence dependent issues so that liability or entitlement is assessed before remedial eligibility and the amount or form of relief.
application_scenario: Use when a claim presents separate questions about breach, fault, status, or entitlement and then asks what relief or compensation follows.
reasoning_flow: Identify the threshold merits issue that must be resolved before any remedy is considered.
Evaluate each required merits element and any complete or partial defense.
Determine which categories of relief become legally available under the merits determination.
Assess causation, remoteness, mitigation, and proof requirements for each available category.
Calculate or structure the remedy by separate heads and combine the issue-level determinations without double counting.
example_application: For an employment dispute, first assess whether termination breached the governing obligations, then identify compensable loss categories, examine mitigation evidence, and calculate each category separately.

template_name: Competing Transaction Characterization
description: Resolve disputes in which the same transfer, payment, or arrangement is assigned competing legal meanings by the parties.
application_scenario: Use when one side characterizes a transaction as a loan, purchase, trust, partnership contribution, agency arrangement, or other legal relationship and the opposing side advances a different characterization.
reasoning_flow: List the competing legal characterizations and the consequences attached to each.
Identify objective indicators such as documents, payment routing, control, possession, repayment terms, and subsequent conduct.
Distinguish contemporaneous evidence from later explanations created after the dispute arose.
Test each characterization against the full course of dealing and applicable presumptions.
Select the characterization that best accounts for the material evidence, then pass that classification to the relevant liability or remedy template.
example_application: Where money was transferred and later claimed back, compare whether the record better reflects a repayable advance, an investment contribution, or property held for another, using contemporaneous communications and control over the funds.

template_name: Temporal Operation of Legal Rules
description: Determine which version of a legal rule applies and whether later repeal, amendment, limitation, or changed circumstances affect an earlier transaction or status.
application_scenario: Use when rights arose under an earlier legal regime, a provision later changed, a limitation period is invoked, or the governing test requires assessment at a particular time.
reasoning_flow: Build a chronology of the legally significant event, accrual of the asserted right, commencement of proceedings, and any relevant legal change.
Identify the default rules on prospectivity, retrospectivity, savings, accrued rights, and limitation.
Determine the legally prescribed assessment date for the issue.
Apply the rule in force at that assessment point while accounting for any transitional or saving provision.
State separately the effect of elapsed time, legal change, and later factual developments.
example_application: For a claim based on a family status formed under an earlier regime, identify when the asserted status and inheritance interest arose, then examine whether a later statutory change altered accrued rights or only future cases.

template_name: Evidence Provenance and Authenticity Assessment
description: Evaluate whether a disputed document, product, shipment, or other item is genuine and connected to the alleged source through a traceable evidentiary chain.
application_scenario: Use when the merits depend on authorship, manufacture, shipment, execution, custody, loss of an original, or another contested source relationship.
reasoning_flow: Define the specific proposition of authenticity, origin, or custody that must be proved.
Identify the party bearing the burden and the applicable standard of proof.
Construct the chain from creation or dispatch through custody, transfer, receipt, and present production.
Assess direct evidence, records, physical or technical indicators, and witness reliability at each link.
Examine alternative sources, breaks in custody, missing originals, and whether any inference or presumption arises.
Record the provenance finding and pass it to the substantive infringement, probate, carriage, or contract analysis.
example_application: When goods are alleged to come from a particular manufacturer, trace purchase and distribution records, compare product features and witness evidence, and test the counterfeiting alternative before addressing infringement.

template_name: Procedural Gateway Before Merits
description: Resolve a procedural threshold that controls whether, where, or in what form the substantive dispute may proceed.
application_scenario: Use for appeals, amendments to a costs bill, consolidation, summary processes, winding-up petitions, or other matters requiring a gateway determination before full merits review.
reasoning_flow: Identify the procedural order sought and the legal threshold governing that order.
Separate the gateway question from the underlying substantive controversy.
Determine whether the applicant has supplied the minimum evidentiary and procedural foundation.
Assess prejudice, duplication, efficiency, finality, and availability of an ordinary trial or alternative procedure where relevant.
Define the permitted scope of further adjudication after the gateway determination.
example_application: In a summary debt-based proceeding, first ask whether the debtor has shown a genuine dispute grounded in substantial evidence; only if the gateway permits should the process move to the requested corporate remedy.

template_name: Discretionary Remedy Balancing
description: Assess whether a claimant who has crossed the merits threshold should receive a discretionary remedy and on what terms.
application_scenario: Use for interim or final injunctions, declarations, validation terms, enforcement orders, buy-out relief, or comparable remedies not granted automatically upon proof of a right.
reasoning_flow: Confirm the legal and evidentiary threshold for considering the requested remedy.
Identify the practical harm to each side if the remedy is imposed or withheld.
Assess adequacy of damages, preservation of the subject matter, urgency, delay, conduct, and enforceability.
Consider effects on third parties and whether narrower terms can reduce unnecessary prejudice.
Formulate proportionate conditions, duration, scope, or safeguards for the remedy.
example_application: For continuation of an asset-preservation order, evaluate the strength of the underlying claim, risk to the assets, hardship to the respondent, adequacy of other relief, and whether tailored exceptions can protect ordinary dealings.

template_name: Corporate Restructuring Stakeholder Safeguards
description: Evaluate a corporate restructuring or insolvency-related request by testing statutory purpose, financial justification, and protection of creditors and other affected stakeholders.
application_scenario: Use for capital reductions, validation orders, winding-up-related terms, rectification, or similar corporate applications affecting the company's asset pool or stakeholder rights.
reasoning_flow: Identify the corporate act requested and the statutory conditions attached to it.
Examine the commercial purpose and whether the proposed act is connected to a legitimate corporate need.
Assess the company's financial position and the effect on the asset pool available to creditors.
Identify creditor notice, consent, security, solvency evidence, and other protective measures.
Check effects on members and third parties, including equality of treatment and procedural regularity.
Specify any safeguards or terms needed to align the corporate act with stakeholder protection.
example_application: For a proposed reduction of capital, examine whether the capital exceeds operational needs, whether the proposal serves a discernible purpose, and whether creditors remain protected through solvency evidence or other safeguards.

template_name: Negligence, Causation, and Shared Fault
description: Analyze an accident by separating breach of duty, factual causation, legal causation, and any contribution by the claimant.
application_scenario: Use in personal injury, road accident, workplace injury, property damage, or nuisance-related cases where multiple acts may have produced the harm.
reasoning_flow: Define the relevant duties and the concrete precautions reasonably required in the circumstances.
Reconstruct the event using location, timing, movement, visibility, warnings, control, and physical-contact evidence.
Determine whether each alleged breach materially contributed to the injury or loss.
Test alternative causal explanations and distinguish the mechanism of contact from the ultimate injury.
Assess whether the claimant's conduct contributed to the harm and, if so, the relative causal responsibility.
Pass the resulting fault allocation to the damages assessment.
example_application: In a pedestrian accident, evaluate vehicle positioning, speed, lookout, warnings, and the pedestrian's own movement, then distinguish whether injury followed from direct contact or an intervening object.

template_name: Structured Damages and Compensation Assessment
description: Assess compensation through separate, non-overlapping heads of loss using evidence appropriate to past, future, pecuniary, and non-pecuniary harm.
application_scenario: Use after liability or statutory entitlement is established in personal injury, fatal accident, employment, trespass, nuisance, or commercial loss disputes.
reasoning_flow: Identify each legally recoverable head of loss and exclude categories outside the pleaded or statutory basis.
Separate past losses from future losses and pecuniary losses from non-pecuniary harm.
Evaluate medical, employment, financial, valuation, and dependency evidence relevant to each head.
Apply causation, remoteness, mitigation, contingencies, and any statutory limits.
Check for overlap among loss categories and adjust for payments or benefits that must be credited.
Aggregate the independently assessed heads into a transparent compensation structure.
example_application: For an injury claim, assess pain and loss of amenities separately from past earnings, future earning capacity, care costs, and expenses, using medical and employment evidence for each category.

template_name: Legal Recognition of Personal or Family Status
description: Determine whether a personal or family relationship receives legal recognition and what succession, probate, or matrimonial consequences follow.
application_scenario: Use when a claim depends on being recognized as a child, adopted child, spouse, beneficiary, or other legally significant family relation.
reasoning_flow: Identify the precise status asserted and the legal consequence for which recognition is sought.
Determine the formal, customary, statutory, or evidentiary requirements for that status.
Examine the relationship's formation, public treatment, household conduct, documentary record, and any competing status claims.
Address temporal changes in recognition rules and any presumptions arising from missing or informal documentation.
Separate the status finding from later questions concerning succession, validity of a testamentary instrument, marital breakdown, or costs.
example_application: Where individuals claim succession rights through a parent-child relationship formed under customary practices, assess the legal recognition requirements and evidence of the relationship before considering entitlement to the estate.

template_name: Documentary Compliance in Commercial Performance
description: Determine whether a commercial document or mode of performance satisfies the governing contractual or rule-based requirements and produces the asserted legal effect.
application_scenario: Use when payment, delivery, transfer, sale, mortgage, or credit obligations depend on the form, contents, presentation, or legal effect of documents.
reasoning_flow: Identify the operative instrument and the exact documentary or performance conditions.
Separate facial compliance of the document from the truth of the underlying transaction unless the governing regime links them.
Compare each required field, signature, description, timing condition, and presentation step with the submitted material.
Assess waiver, variation, course of dealing, substitution, and any discrepancy claimed by the opposing party.
Determine the legal consequence of each material discrepancy and pass that determination to the payment, ownership, or enforcement analysis.
example_application: For a documentary payment dispute, compare the presented transport record with the instrument's stated requirements, distinguish document examination from the underlying shipment, and assess whether any discrepancy was waived.

template_name: Decompose and Order Interdependent Issues
description: Break a compound dispute into separately answerable legal issues, identify which issues are threshold questions and which depend on earlier findings, and combine the issue-level conclusions in a legally coherent order.
application_scenario: Use when a case presents several questions concerning liability, entitlement, procedure, defenses, valuation, or remedy, especially where one question must be resolved before another becomes material.
reasoning_flow: List each distinct legal issue without merging factual and remedial questions.
Classify each issue as threshold, merits, defense, valuation, or remedy.
Identify dependencies among issues and place prerequisite questions first.
Resolve each issue under its own rule, material facts, and burden.
Combine the issue-level conclusions while preserving any conditional dependencies.
example_application: A dispute involves authority to entertain the claim, the existence of an underlying entitlement, a limitation defense, and the amount of relief. Analyze authority first, then entitlement and defenses, and address amount only if the earlier questions make it necessary.

template_name: Filter and Map Material Facts
description: Reduce a lengthy factual record to the facts that bear on each legal element, while separating background, duplicated allegations, and facts relevant only to another issue.
application_scenario: Use when the record contains many events, documents, communications, payments, or procedural steps and only a subset is legally material to a particular issue.
reasoning_flow: State the legal issue and its elements before reviewing the factual record.
Tag each fact by the element or procedural question it may affect.
Separate direct evidence, contextual evidence, adverse evidence, and immaterial background.
Resolve inconsistencies and avoid counting repeated descriptions as independent proof.
Produce an issue-specific fact set that includes both favorable and unfavorable material.
example_application: In a dispute over the nature of a payment and later conduct, map transfer records, contemporaneous communications, accounting treatment, and repayment behavior to the competing characterizations, while excluding unrelated dealings.

template_name: Extract and Operationalize a Supplied Rule
description: Convert a supplied statute, ordinance, procedural rule, or contractual provision into an operational test that can be applied element by element.
application_scenario: Use when the governing source is identified in the materials but the legal test must still be reconstructed from its text, structure, exceptions, and discretionary language.
reasoning_flow: Identify the operative provision and the legal consequence it regulates.
Separate mandatory prerequisites, definitions, exceptions, presumptions, and discretionary factors.
Translate each requirement into a concrete factual question.
Assign the burden and standard of proof where the source or doctrine provides them.
Apply the requirements in sequence and record which remain contested or fact-dependent.
example_application: A statutory application requires a qualifying status, specified procedural steps, and consideration of affected persons. Convert those requirements into separate factual checks before assessing the requested order.

template_name: Identify and Complete the Governing Doctrine
description: Determine the appropriate legal doctrine when the materials state the dispute but do not supply a complete rule, then formulate only the portions of the doctrine needed for the issues presented.
application_scenario: Use when a claim concerns negligence, contractual characterization, restraint, restitution, property entitlement, or another familiar doctrine but the governing test is not expressly provided.
reasoning_flow: Classify the claim, defense, and requested remedy by their legal function rather than their labels alone.
Identify the doctrine or doctrines that govern the pleaded facts.
State the minimum elements and any recognized exceptions relevant to the dispute.
Check whether a competing doctrine better fits the same facts or remedy.
Apply the selected doctrine without importing elements unrelated to the actual issues.
example_application: A payment is described differently by the parties and the materials provide no express test. Identify the doctrines governing loans, gifts, investments, and restitution, then compare the facts against the elements that distinguish those categories.

template_name: Test Precedent Fit by Analogy and Distinction
description: Use prior decisions to derive a transferable principle, compare the legally significant facts, and explain whether differences alter the principle's application.
application_scenario: Use when the parties rely on earlier decisions concerning similar procedural powers, statutory criteria, evidentiary questions, remedies, or fact patterns.
reasoning_flow: Extract the rule or factor from the prior decision rather than copying its result.
Identify the material facts that made the precedent applicable.
Compare those facts and the governing legal context with the present dispute.
Distinguish differences that affect an element, policy, burden, or available remedy.
State the degree and limits of the precedent's guidance for the current issue.
example_application: A prior decision approved a procedural technique under particular safeguards. Compare the volume of material, proportionality concerns, reliability controls, and opportunities for challenge before using its reasoning in a new proceeding.

template_name: Allocate Burdens and Assess Evidentiary Sufficiency
description: Identify who must prove each proposition, assess the quality and consistency of the evidence, and determine whether the record is sufficient at the applicable procedural stage.
application_scenario: Use when liability, status, kinship, ownership, negligence, misconduct, or another disputed fact depends on testimony, documents, expert material, inferences, or competing accounts.
reasoning_flow: Assign the burden for each disputed proposition and identify the applicable standard.
Separate admissibility, credibility, weight, and legal sufficiency.
Compare contemporaneous documents, objective circumstances, and testimonial consistency.
Address missing evidence and whether an adverse inference is legally available.
Evaluate whether the evidence meets the burden for the current stage of the proceeding.
example_application: A party claims a legal status based on personal history and records while the opposing party presents an arguable alternative account. Assess authenticity, consistency, corroboration, and the burden appropriate to the stage.

template_name: Screen Procedural Gateways Before the Merits
description: Resolve procedural conditions that control whether and how the merits may be examined, including jurisdiction, standing, pleading sufficiency, limitation, joinder, amendment, and abuse of process.
application_scenario: Use when a case contains a preliminary objection or procedural application that may narrow, postpone, reshape, or preclude merits analysis.
reasoning_flow: Identify the procedural rule and the consequence of failing its threshold.
Determine the procedural stage and the standard applicable at that stage.
Test jurisdiction, standing, timeliness, pleading sufficiency, party structure, or process integrity as relevant.
Distinguish curable defects from defects that cannot be cured within the proceeding.
Define the scope of merits analysis that remains after the procedural ruling.
example_application: Before examining the substance of a claim, determine whether the tribunal has authority, whether the claimant has standing, whether sufficient material facts are pleaded, and whether any proposed amendment falls within the permitted factual foundation.

template_name: Evaluate Defenses and Counterarguments Element by Element
description: Treat each affirmative defense or counterargument as a distinct legal test, identify its proponent's burden, and examine how it interacts with the primary claim.
application_scenario: Use when the response invokes matters such as contributory fault, justification, privilege, estoppel, waiver, acquiescence, abuse of process, or equitable unfairness.
reasoning_flow: List each defense separately and identify whether it negates an element, creates an exception, or limits relief.
State the elements and burden associated with the defense.
Map the defense-specific facts and evidence without reusing the primary claim's conclusion.
Test any reply, exception, or loss of the defense.
Integrate the defense with the primary claim and identify its effect on liability, scope, or remedy.
example_application: A claimant establishes a prima facie wrong, while the respondent raises several distinct defenses based on truth, protected occasion, and the claimant's own conduct. Analyze each defense under its own elements and evidentiary basis.

template_name: Resolve Competing Legal Characterizations
description: Choose among competing legal classifications by examining objective features, contemporaneous conduct, legal consequences, and the consistency of each classification with the whole record.
application_scenario: Use when the dispute turns on whether a transaction, relationship, payment, client status, membership, or property arrangement falls into one of several legal categories.
reasoning_flow: List the competing classifications and the legal consequences of each.
Identify the features that legally distinguish the categories.
Examine documents, conduct, control, risk allocation, expectations, and accounting treatment.
Give limited weight to labels that conflict with the transaction's substance.
Select the characterization that best explains the material facts and then apply its legal consequences.
example_application: The same transfer is described as a loan, investment contribution, adjustment, or gift. Compare repayment expectations, risk sharing, documentation, later demands, and how the parties recorded the transfer.

template_name: Stage Entitlement Before Valuation or Quantum
description: Separate the existence and scope of legal entitlement from the later calculation of damages, compensation, reserve value, or another monetary measure.
application_scenario: Use when a case combines liability or statutory entitlement questions with a distinct assessment of monetary relief or property value.
reasoning_flow: Determine whether the legal basis for liability or entitlement is established.
Identify any apportionment, causation, mitigation, or scope limits that affect the compensable interest.
Select the legally appropriate valuation date and measure.
Evaluate the relevant factual and expert inputs for each component of the calculation.
Calculate or frame the quantum without double counting and explain any contingencies.
example_application: A personal injury or property proceeding first requires a finding of responsibility or statutory entitlement, followed by separate assessment of loss components or market-based values using the proper measure and date.

template_name: Apply Discretion Through Structured Fairness and Proportionality
description: Exercise a discretionary procedural or substantive power by identifying its purpose, relevant factors, prejudice to affected parties, proportionality, and possible safeguards.
application_scenario: Use when the court may allow an amendment, extension, adjournment, joinder, possession order, interim payment, removal, or other relief after threshold requirements are met.
reasoning_flow: Identify the source, purpose, and limits of the discretionary power.
List legally relevant factors and exclude considerations unrelated to that purpose.
Assess prejudice, delay, costs, good faith, practical feasibility, and effects on third parties.
Consider whether conditions or narrower relief can reduce unfairness.
Balance the factors transparently and state the scope of the discretionary response.
example_application: A party seeks additional time or permission to alter its case. Examine the explanation, timing, effect on the opposing party, case-management consequences, and whether conditions can preserve procedural fairness.

template_name: Combine Statutory Compliance with Stakeholder Protection
description: Assess an application that requires both formal statutory compliance and substantive protection of creditors, tenants, minority owners, beneficiaries, or other affected persons.
application_scenario: Use in corporate, insolvency, property, probate, or restructuring matters where the applicant must satisfy prescribed steps and show that the proposal is financially feasible, fair, or non-prejudicial.
reasoning_flow: Identify the applicant's formal and substantive statutory prerequisites.
Verify notices, approvals, ownership thresholds, financial capacity, and other required steps.
Identify each affected stakeholder group and the interests the law protects.
Assess prejudice, compensation, fairness of terms, and available safeguards.
Evaluate the proposal as a whole, including feasibility and compliance with the statutory purpose.
example_application: An organization seeks approval for a restructuring or property-related order. Check procedural compliance and financial feasibility, then examine whether creditors or other affected holders receive adequate protection and fair treatment.
